title: Application of bedside ultrasound guidance in difficult diagnostic lumbar puncture in infectious diseases: Technical specifications, clinical evidence, and practical prospects.
abstract: Diagnostic lumbar puncture is a core procedure in the diagnosis and management of infectious diseases. However, in patients with complex anatomical conditions, such as obesity and spinal deformities, the traditional blind puncture method is often challenging to perform, resulting in a substantially higher failure rates and increased complication risks. Bedside ultrasound guidance provides a precise, visual solution to these challenges and represents an emerging tool for improving clinical practice. This narrative review aimed to comprehensively examine the clinical value of ultrasound-guided lumbar puncture in infectious diseases, focusing on the current evidence base, core ultrasound technical principles, standardized pre-puncture assessment procedures, and clinical implementation strategies. Furthermore, it sought to empower infectious disease physicians to utilize safe, efficient, and scalable auxiliary techniques while outlining future directions. Compared with traditional landmark-based methods, ultrasound guidance significantly improves the first-attempt puncture success rate by approximately 20%-30%. Its key technical advantages include real-time visualization of the needle tip, identification of the optimal insertion point, and reduction of procedural complications.

title: High-Grade Percutaneous Medial Collateral Ligament Pie-Crusting Is Not Associated With Clinically Meaningful Valgus Instability.
abstract: Background Medial collateral ligament (MCL) pie-crusting is used during medial meniscal surgery to improve visualization and reduce the risk of chondral injuries. However, some surgeons extend the release site beyond routine incremental perforation, and the effect of this more extensive release on postoperative medial laxity remains unclear. Purpose To determine whether high-grade percutaneous MCL pie-crusting during medial meniscus posterior root tear (MMPRT) repair results in clinically meaningful valgus instability postoperatively as assessed by valgus stress radiography. Study design Case series; Level of evidence, 4. Methods A retrospective review was performed of patients who underwent isolated MMPRT repair with high-grade MCL pie-crusting and no prior knee ligament surgery. High-grade pie-crusting was defined intraoperatively by an audible and palpable release and a substantial medial compartment opening (≥6 mm) under arthroscopic visualization. Postoperative bilateral valgus stress radiographs were obtained at a mean of 5.9 ± 2.0 months with the knee positioned at 20° of flexion. Gapping was measured in millimeters, and the side-to-side difference was calculated using the contralateral knee as an internal control. An a priori power analysis based on a 3.2-mm threshold for clinically meaningful medial-sided laxity demonstrated a required sample size of 15 patients. The side-to-side difference in medial compartment gapping was analyzed using the 1-sample t test compared with the 3.2-mm threshold. Results A total of 21 patients met inclusion criteria. The mean medial compartment gapping was 7.84 ± 1.65 mm in the operative knee and 6.62 ± 1.37 mm in the contralateral knee. The mean side-to-side difference was 1.21 ± 1.07 mm (95% CI, 0.73-1.70 mm). The observed difference was significantly less than the 3.2-mm threshold associated with clinically meaningful medial-sided instability ( P < .001). Conclusion High-grade percutaneous MCL pie-crusting advanced to a defined intraoperative endpoint during MMPRT repair resulted in small increases in medial compartment gapping that remained below biomechanically defined instability thresholds. These preliminary findings suggest that high-grade MCL pie-crusting improves visualization and instrumentation without being associated with clinically meaningful valgus laxity postoperatively.

title: Pretreatment MRI radiomics for predicting recurrence and metastasis after hypofractionated stereotactic radiosurgery in uveal melanoma.
abstract: PurposeTo develop and internally evaluate pretreatment MR-based radiomics models for predicting local recurrence and metastasis after hypofractionated stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) for uveal melanoma.MethodsThis retrospective study analyzed pretreatment MRI (T1-weighted, T2-weighted, contrast-enhanced T1-weighted) of 88 SRS-treated UM patients. Tumors were segmented on the axial slice with the greatest cross-sectional area, and 854 radiomic features were extracted for each sequence. After inter-observer reproducibility filtering (ICC ≥ 0.80) and elastic-net feature selection, separate Gaussian Naive Bayes models for local recurrence and metastasis were developed using the retained features with a 70:30 train-test split. SMOTE was applied within training folds to address class imbalance. Held-out test set performance was assessed using AUC, F1 score, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values.ResultsThe local-recurrence model achieved an AUC of 0.958, accuracy of 0.889, sensitivity of 1.00 (3/3), and specificity of 0.875 (21/24). The metastasis model showed limited discrimination (AUC, 0.528; accuracy, 0.815; sensitivity, 0.333 [1/3]; specificity, 0.875 [21/24]). Among three-fraction treatments, a total dose >45 Gy was associated with less local recurrence ( p = 0.010), whereas no other clinical variable was significantly associated with either outcome.ConclusionMRI radiomics showed promising discrimination for local recurrence but limited discrimination for metastasis. These findings should be interpreted with caution given the small number of events in the test set and warrant external validation in larger cohorts .

title: Baseline Knee Extension Is Associated With Volumetric Femoral Cartilage Loss in the Central Region of the Mid-lateral and External Medial Femoral Condyles: Data From the Osteoarthritis Initiative.
abstract: ObjectiveData evaluating knee flexion contracture (FC)-associated regional changes on femoral articular cartilage are lacking. We compared regional femoral articular cartilage outcomes of people with knee osteoarthritis (OA) with and without FC using quantitative MRI data.MethodsArticular cartilage of the medial and lateral femoral condyles were segmented into internal, central, and external subregions on MRI. Goniometry measured knee extension. We tested for regional differences in cartilage thickness and percent denuded bone (i.e., 0mm cartilage thickness) in the presence or absence of FC, and for associations between cartilage outcomes with quantitative knee extension range of motion (ROM) using a linear model for 596 participants.ResultsFor FC versus no FC, cartilage thickness in the central lateral subregion was higher (2.36±0.42mm vs. 2.29±0.43mm; p<0.05), with higher percent denuded bone in the central lateral (0.92±3.5% vs. 0.39±2.2%; p<0.05) and central medial subregions (4.61±12.88% vs. 3.17±11.66%; p<0.05). Lost knee extension was associated with increased percent denuded bone in the internal lateral ( r= 0.095; p<0.05), central lateral ( r =0.90; p<0.05), and central medial subregions ( r =0.117 ; p<0.01) but with increased central lateral cartilage thickness ( r =0.110; p<0.01). After correcting for clinical factors, an association between lost knee extension and increased percent denuded bone remained in the central lateral femur [ β =0.059; (95% CI 0.003-0.114)].ConclusionConclusion: Lost knee extension was associated with increased percent denuded bone in the central lateral and external medial femur. Interventions to maintain and/or restore knee ROM may benefit femoral cartilage health. Longitudinal studies evaluating the impact of lost knee ROM on femoral cartilage are warranted.

title: Who participates in LDCT screening for the early detection of lung cancer after long-term occupational exposure to asbestos dust? Results of the analysis of administrative and medical routine data from the German Social Accident Insurance.
abstract: Background Lung cancer is one of the most common cancers in Germany and is predominantly detected at an advanced stage. To ensure early detection, the German Social Accident Insurance (DGUV) offers lung cancer screening including a low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) for individuals with long-term occupational exposure to asbestos dust and a smoking history of at least 30 pack years. However, evidence remains scarce about what encourages this group of people to participate in LDCT screening after medical consultation. Methods A secondary data analysis using routinely collected medical and administrative data between 2014 and 2024 was conducted in a cross-sectional design. This study aimed to investigate factors that could be used to predict the uptake of LDCT screening following a medical consultation. Exploratory logistic regression analysis was used to identify and assess possible predictors. Results The sample included n = 14,491 individuals (97% male; average age 67 years; average asbestos dust exposure 21 years; average cigarette consumption 43 pack years). 74% of individuals underwent LDCT screening after medical consultation. 13 predictors were included in the regression model. The model demonstrated a low level of variance explanation (Nagelkerkes R 2 = 0.026). Younger individuals (OR: 0.96, p < 0.001), individuals with prolonged exposure to asbestos dust (OR: 1.01, p = 0.011) and with a history of pneumonia (OR: 1.16, p = 0.011) were more likely to undergo LDCT screening. Conclusion The predictors showed only a low explanatory power. Further research should include non-participants and expand the exploratory model to include theoretically grounded predictors.

title: Effect of injectable platelet rich fibrin augmented with vitamin c compared to injectable platelet rich fibrin alone on healing of necrotic mature single rooted teeth with chronic periapical periodontitis following regenerative endodontic therapy (a randomized controlled trial).
abstract: Objectives To assess the healing potential, postoperative pain and clinical normalcy associated with injectable platelet-rich fibrin combined with Vitamin C in regenerative endodontic procedure using cone-beam computed tomography and two-dimensional radiograph. Methods Twenty-eight healthy patients with mature permanent single-rooted teeth diagnosed with pulp necrosis and chronic apical periodontitis were randomly allocated into two groups (n = 14). Regenerative endodontic treatment was performed using injectable platelet-rich fibrin combined with Vitamin C (intervention group) and injectable platelet-rich fibrin alone (control group). Periapical healing was assessed using CBCT and periapical radiographs over 12 months. Postoperative pain and clinical normalcy were also evaluated. Results Both groups showed significant lesion reduction at 12 months (P = 0.001), with no significant between-group differences in postoperative lesion size (P = 0.981) or reduction magnitude (P = 0.497). CBCT-PAI scores improved in both groups without significant intergroup differences at baseline or follow-up. Two-dimensional radiographs showed a baseline difference (P = 0.007) but no postoperative differences; both groups demonstrated significant longitudinal reduction (P < 0.001). Postoperative pain scores were comparable between groups at all time points (P > 0.05), with a significant temporal decrease observed only in the intervention group (P = 0.001). All teeth remained asymptomatic during follow-up. Conclusions Both i-PRF combined with vitamin C and i-PRF alone appear to be effective regenerative scaffolds, demonstrating comparable clinical and radiographic outcomes in regenerative endodontic procedures. Clinical trial registration The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (ID: NCT05585359), registered on 14 October 2022. Available at https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05585359 .

title: Colour maps for representation of quantitative metrics in radiology: meaningful or misleading?
abstract: The increased utility of quantitative metrics in medical imaging has prompted the use of colour representation of the data. Colour schemes for image display can highlight pathology and distinguish normal anatomy, thus potentially aiding image interpretation. Adding colour schemes to images may serve the sole purpose of visualising an abnormality or may seek to represent and meaningfully convey a quantitative metric. An early use of colour representation is exemplified by colour Doppler in ultrasound (US), where a two-sided linear scale is commonly applied. More recently, many schemes have arisen, ranging from a single colour to depict a segmented region to a range of colours that embrace the entire colour spectrum. These may be applied as continuous or discrete palettes, depending on the software vendor or even on individual user settings. The lack of standardisation of colour schemes across the medical community, especially in medical imaging, risks misinterpretation of quantitative data and potential unintended negative clinical consequences. The purpose of this article is to review the colour schemes used for quantitative imaging across US, computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and positron emission tomography (PET), the way in which they are applied, the clinical applications where their use is desirable for enhanced interpretation, and the pitfalls where standardisation is lacking in a variety of clinical applications. Finally, we discuss some solutions that could be employed to enable standardisation and augment the use of colour in image interpretation. KEY POINTS: Question Colour schemes in medical imaging can highlight pathology, but standardisation is lacking for most imaging modalities, thus risking misinterpretation of quantitative data. Findings For T1, T2, and T2* maps and their inverses, colour map recommendations have recently been proposed, but are mostly lacking for other quantitative data. Critical relevance statement Standardised colour maps can enhance data analyses across scanners and institutions, which is important for multicentre studies and handling big data. Furthermore, standardised and harmonised colour maps could improve lesion conspicuity, cross-platform comparability, and longitudinal reliability.

title: Phase-adaptive automated whole-liver quantification of signal intensity-derived liver indices from gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI.
abstract: Objectives To develop and validate a phase-adaptive pipeline for automated whole-liver, parenchyma-based quantification of signal intensity-derived liver indices from gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI without inter-phase co-registration. Materials and methods In this retrospective, single-center study (2016-2025), 9,013 liver MRI examinations were screened, and 3,112 gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI examinations were identified. The first examination per patient defined the clinical cohort (1,174 patients; mean age, 59.6 ± 14 years [range, 4-93 years]; 611 men). A phase-adaptive nnU-Net was trained on 403 and tested on 500 dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI sequences for segmentation of liver parenchyma, intrahepatic non-parenchymal structures, and spleen; paraspinal muscle reference regions were obtained using TotalSegmentator. Segmentation accuracy was assessed against manually corrected reference segmentations generated by a semi-automatic annotation workflow with Dice similarity coefficients. Automated arterial enhancement fraction (AEF), relative liver enhancement (RLE), hepatocellular uptake index (HUI), liver-to-spleen ratio (LSR), and liver-to-muscle ratio (LMR) were compared with manual region-of-interest measurements in a radiological validation cohort (50 patients) using intraclass correlation coefficients and Bland-Altman analysis. Liver indices were compared between patients with cirrhotic and non-cirrhotic livers using the Mann-Whitney U-test. Results Liver parenchyma segmentation achieved Dice similarity coefficients of 0.998-0.999. Reader-model agreement for the liver indices ranged from 0.936 to 0.977. HUI, LSR, RLE, and LMR were lower in cirrhosis (p < 0.001), whereas AEF did not differ (p = 0.14). Conclusion Phase-adaptive segmentation enables whole-liver quantification of signal intensity-derived liver indices without inter-phase co-registration. The lower hepatobiliary uptake indices in cirrhosis support the plausibility of this approach for scalable quantitative assessment of liver MRI. Key points Question Can gadoxetic acid-enhanced liver MRI be quantified automatically across contrast phases without inter-phase co-registration or manual region-of-interest placement in routine clinical imaging? Findings Phase-adaptive segmentation enabled automated whole-liver quantification with liver Dice coefficients of 0.998-0.999 and excellent agreement with manual measurements for five liver indices. Relevance Statement Automated whole-liver quantification from standard gadoxetic acid-enhanced liver MRI provides reproducible, signal-intensity-derived liver indices and reduces dependence on manual region-of-interest measurements in large-scale clinical studies.

title: CT-based multi-station lymph-node radiomics for preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis in colorectal cancer: a proof-of-concept comparison with primary-tumor radiomics.
abstract: Objective Accurate preoperative prediction of lymph node metastasis (LNM) in colorectal cancer remains challenging using conventional CT assessment. This proof-of-concept study compared CT-based multi-station lymph-node radiomics with primary-tumor radiomics for patient-level preoperative prediction of LNM. Materials and methods This single-center retrospective study included patients with pathologically confirmed colorectal cancer who underwent preoperative contrast-enhanced CT and surgical resection. Patients were divided into training and validation cohorts. Radiomics features were extracted from the primary tumor and visible regional lymph nodes across multiple nodal stations. Three radiomics strategies were developed and compared: primary-tumor radiomics, multi-station lymph-node radiomics, and combined radiomics. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration analysis, decision curve analysis, and five-fold cross-validation. Pairwise AUCs were compared using the DeLong test. A clinical-radiomic model was further constructed by integrating the optimal radiomics strategy with preoperative clinical variables. Results In the validation cohort, the multi-station lymph-node radiomics model outperformed the primary-tumor radiomics model for predicting LNM (AUC, 0.864 versus 0.637; p = 0.0055). The combined radiomics model achieved an AUC of 0.840, without significant improvement over the lymph-node model (p = 0.2211). After integration with clinical variables, the clinical-radiomic model achieved an AUC of 0.879. Conclusion CT-based multi-station lymph-node radiomics showed significantly higher validation performance than primary-tumor radiomics for patient-level preoperative LNM prediction in colorectal cancer. However, this single-center proof-of-concept model is not ready for direct clinical implementation and requires multicenter external validation before clinical translation. Key points Question Can CT-based multi-station lymph-node radiomics improve preoperative nodal metastasis prediction beyond primary-tumor radiomics in patients with surgically treated colorectal cancer? Findings Multi-station lymph-node radiomics achieved higher validation performance than primary-tumor radiomics for patient-level prediction of pathological lymph-node metastasis in colorectal cancer. Relevance statement CT-based multi-station lymph-node radiomics may support individualized preoperative nodal risk stratification in colorectal cancer, but multicenter validation and prospective evaluation are required before clinical translation.

title: Adapting Segment Anything Model 3 for concept-driven lesion segmentation in medical images: an experimental study.
abstract: Accurate segmentation of lesions is fundamental for medical image analysis. However, most existing approaches are designed for specific anatomical sites and imaging modalities, limiting their applicability in heterogeneous clinical environments. Recent vision-language foundation models have enabled concept-driven segmentation of natural images, offering a promising path toward more flexible and generalizable medical image segmentation. However, to the best of the authors' knowledge, concept-prompt-based lesion segmentation in medical images, particularly using the latest Segment Anything Model 3 (SAM3), has not been thoroughly examined. In this paper, the authors present a systematic investigation of the SAM3 framework for lesion segmentation. An extensive evaluation of SAM3 was first conducted using geometric bounding boxes and concept-based text and image exemplars as prompts for lesion segmentation across multiple cancer types and imaging modalities, including magnetic resonance imaging, computed tomography, ultrasound, dermoscopy, and endoscopic imaging, with particular emphasis on volumetric medical imaging datasets. To improve robustness and segmentation accuracy, additional knowledge into the input representation was further integrated, including predictions from adjacent slices, multiparametric imaging information, and prior annotations. In addition, the study compared different SAM3 fine-tuning strategies on the BraTS2023-MET dataset, including partial module fine-tuning, adapter-based optimization, and full-model fine-tuning, under different training objectives. Extensive experiments conducted on 13 datasets covering 11 lesion types demonstrate that SAM3 achieves strong cross-modality generalization and accurate instance-specific lesion delineation. These results highlight the potential of concept-driven foundation models for scalable and practical medical-image segmentation in real-world clinical settings. The source code and dataset splits are publicly available at https://github.com/apple1986/lesion-sam3 .

title: Hodgkin Lymphoma With Sarcoid-Like Reaction: Importance of Clinicopathological Correlation in Granulomatous Lymphadenopathy.
abstract: BACKGROUND Sarcoid-like reaction, characterized by noncaseating epithelioid granulomas, occurs in 13.8% of Hodgkin lymphoma cases. When the granulomatous component is prominent and neoplastic cells are scarce, the initial biopsy may lead to a misdiagnosis of sarcoidosis. Reliance on pathological findings alone, without integration of the clinical context, can result in considerable diagnostic delay. CASE REPORT A 63-year-old man with systemic lymphadenopathy underwent cervical lymph node biopsy, which showed epithelioid granulomas without identifiable neoplastic cells. Sarcoidosis was initially suspected based on the pathological findings. However, comprehensive evaluation revealed no typical manifestations of sarcoidosis, including bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, uveitis, or elevated serum angiotensin-converting enzyme levels. The discordance between the pathological diagnosis and clinical findings led us to retain malignant lymphoma in the differential diagnosis. During follow-up, the patient developed B symptoms with substantially elevated soluble interleukin-2 receptor levels. Repeat biopsy of the left supraclavicular lymph node, performed 7 months after the initial presentation, revealed Reed-Sternberg-like multinucleated cells surrounded by a sarcoid-like reaction, confirming classical Hodgkin lymphoma. CONCLUSIONS This case illustrates that pathological findings alone may be insufficient for a definitive diagnosis of granulomatous lymphadenopathy. Malignant lymphoma should remain in the differential diagnosis, even when the initial biopsy suggests sarcoidosis. When clinical features are inconsistent with the pathological diagnosis, clinicians should reconsider the differential diagnosis, and repeat biopsy may be warranted. Integration of clinical findings, imaging, and histopathology is important to avoid diagnostic delay.

title: Brought with the wind: A case of melioidosis acquired in the United States presenting with multiple pulmonary nodules.
abstract: Burkholderia pseudomallei, the causative agent of melioidosis, is a gram-negative bacterium historically endemic to Southeast Asia and Northern Australia. However, recent environmental detection along the Gulf Coast and an increasing number of reported cases in non-travelers have raised questions regarding potential endemicity and environmental establishment in the Southern United States. We report a case of putatively locally acquired pulmonary melioidosis in a Florida resident with no recent international travel history, illustrating the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges posed by this rare pathogen. The patient presented with fever, pleuritic chest pain, and hypoxia following a period of severe weather. Computed tomography (CT) of the chest revealed multiple solid pulmonary nodules with ground-glass opacities and mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Given his underlying stage 3b chronic kidney disease (CKD), the patient was treated with an intensive course of intravenous ceftazidime followed by oral doxycycline monotherapy, achieving full clinical recovery. Follow-up imaging at 3 months demonstrated complete resolution of the pulmonary nodules. This case emphasizes the importance of considering melioidosis in the differential diagnosis for non-resolving community-acquired pneumonia or significant pulmonary nodules in the Southern United States, even in the absence of international travel. Risk factors such as diabetes mellitus and severe weather events are key clinical clues. While trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole remains the preferred eradication therapy, doxycycline may serve as a potential alternative for patients with renal impairment when first-line therapy is contraindicated.

title: ReViT-RF: A hybrid ResNet-50-Vision Transformer with a Radiomic Feature Fusion framework for lung tumor classification and TNM-based stage prediction using CT images.
abstract: Lung cancer is one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, emphasizing the need for accurate, automated, and clinically interpretable diagnostic systems. Although existing deep learning (DL) models have achieved promising performance in classifying lung nodules as benign or malignant, most approaches are limited to binary classification and provide insufficient support for detailed tumor characterization and TNM staging. Furthermore, conventional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are effective in extracting local morphological features but often fail to capture long-range spatial dependencies. In contrast, transformer-based models can learn global contextual information but may compromise fine-grained local feature representation. To address these limitations, this study proposes a hybrid ResNet-50-Vision Transformer with Radiomic Feature Fusion (ReViT-RF) framework for lung tumor classification and component-wise TNM stage prediction using thoracic computed tomography (CT) images from the publicly available Lung Image Database Consortium and Image Database Resource Initiative (LIDC-IDRI) dataset. The primary clinical objectives of the proposed framework are to: (i) classify pulmonary nodules as benign or malignant, and (ii) predict individual TNM components, including primary tumor extent (T), lymph node involvement (N), and metastatic status (M) for malignant cases. To improve tumor visibility and image quality, CT images are initially preprocessed using Contrast-Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) and intensity normalization. The proposed ReViT-RF architecture integrates the complementary advantages of ResNet-50 and Vision Transformer (ViT) for comprehensive feature learning. The CNN branch extracts local morphological, textural, and structural characteristics, whereas the transformer branch captures long-range spatial relationships and global contextual dependencies. In addition, handcrafted radiomic features, including shape, size, texture, and spatial descriptors, are fused with deep features to provide clinically meaningful information for accurate TNM component prediction. The dataset is divided into training, validation, and testing subsets using an 80:10:10 ratio, with data augmentation applied only to the training set to prevent information leakage. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 97.62% for benign-malignant classification, along with high precision, recall, and F1-score values. Moreover, independent prediction of TNM components provides detailed stage-related information rather than relying on a single aggregated stage label, enabling more precise tumor assessment and clinical decision support. Furthermore, explainability analysis using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) identifies the critical tumor regions contributing to model predictions, improving interpretability and enhancing clinician confidence. Overall, by combining hybrid deep feature extraction, radiomic feature fusion, component-wise TNM stage prediction, and explainable AI analysis, the proposed ReViT-RF framework provides a reliable, comprehensive, and clinically interpretable solution for automated lung tumor analysis.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of preoperative magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography in delineating biliary anatomy in live liver donors: An ambispective observational study.
abstract: Backgrounds/aims Accurate preoperative delineation of biliary anatomy is essential for living donor liver transplantation (LDLT), as unrecognised variants contribute to biliary complications. This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) for characterising biliary anatomy in live donors, using intraoperative cholangiography (IOC) as the reference standard. Methods An ambispective observational study included 89 live liver donors (65 retrospective, 24 prospective) at a tertiary LDLT centre. Biliary anatomy was classified on MRCP and IOC using the Huang classification. Variant anatomy (Huang types A2-A5) was defined as the positive test condition and standard anatomy (A1) as the negative condition. Diagnostic performance was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, and Cohen's kappa. Results The cohort comprised 58 females (65.2%) and 31 males (34.8%), with a mean age of 34.34 ± 9.53 years. Huang type A1 was most common on MRCP (65.2%) and IOC (59.6%), while variants (A2-A5) were detected in 34.8% and 40.4%, respectively. Against IOC, MRCP showed 77.78% sensitivity (95% CI, 61.92%-88.28%), 94.34% specificity (95% CI, 84.63%-98.06%), 90.32% positive predictive value (95% CI, 75.10%-96.65%), 86.21% negative predictive value (95% CI, 75.07%-92.84%), and 87.64% overall accuracy, with substantial agreement (κ = 0.737, p < 0.001). Conclusions MRCP is highly specific for preoperative biliary mapping in LDLT donors but has limited sensitivity for variants, supporting routine IOC before ductal transection.

title: Multiple classification of childhood and juvenile autism spectrum disorder from ABIDE-II sMRI using BN-GO-CNN.
abstract: Objectives Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) shows heterogeneous neurodevelopmental patterns across childhood, juvenile development, and adulthood, so binary MRI classification may not fully capture age-and sex-related variation. This study proposes a proof-of-concept framework for multiple classification using ABIDE-II T1-weighted structural MRI (sMRI). Methods After image-quality screening, sMRI slices were processed using Canny edge detection, brain-region cropping, 224 × 224 resizing, and augmentation. Images were organized into sex-based four-class, age-based four-class, and combined age-and-sex eight-class datasets, separating child, young, juvenile, adult, male, and female groups. A Batch-Normalized Grid-Optimized CNN (BN-GO-CNN) was developed to learn structural representations directly from preprocessed sMRI, with grid search used to select key CNN hyperparameters. The model was compared with VGG16, DenseNet201, MobileNetV2, and EfficientNet-B0 using identical image partitions. Results BN-GO-CNN achieved validation accuracies of 67.0 %, 64.0 %, and 60.5 % for sex-based, age-based, and combined age-and-sex classification, respectively. These outcomes remained above chance but showed limited class separability. Conclusions The modest performance suggests that label-related sMRI differences are subtle, supporting this framework as a preliminary test of CNN-assisted sMRI classification for future research use rather than a clinically reliable ASD diagnostic system.

title: Deco-CLIP: Dual-Branch Feature Decoupling CLIP for Fine-Grained Zero-Shot Medical Image Analysis
abstract: Abstract The CLIP model has been widely used in the medical field, improving the efficiency of disease screening and diagnosis by establishing feature-level associations between medical images and radiology reports. However, we have found that the contrastive learning strategy of current medical CLIP primarily focuses on distinguishing high-level semantic features. Therefore, it fails to capture the low-level features related to attributes and relational information, limiting performance in fine-grained tasks. To address these limitations, we propose Deco-CLIP to decouple representational features from semantic features. Specifically, the image modality consists of two Vision Transformer (ViT) encoders that extract semantic and texture features using different pretraining strategies. The text modality consists of a text encoder with dual branches to focus on tokens representing high- and low-level features. Furthermore, to enhance the model's ability to capture fine-grained features, we propose a threshold-adaptive sample mining strategy based on intra-modal similarity, which clusters semantically similar samples into mini-batches. Then, secondary contrastive learning is applied within the mini-batch to align the fine-grained features between image and text modalities. Additionally, a regularized attention mechanism is proposed to guide the two branches of the text encoder to focus on distinct feature representations. We evaluated Deco-CLIP on fine-grained zero-shot tasks, including multi-abnormality detection and report-to-volume retrieval. The results showed a 10.2\% improvement in accuracy for multi-abnormality detection and a 16.2\% increase in recall for report-to-volume retrieval, demonstrating the effectiveness of Deco-CLIP in fine-grained medical tasks. The code will be publicly released.

title: The Saturation Gap as a Diagnostic Clue for Methemoglobinemia in a Child with Persistent Low Oxygen Saturation
abstract: Abstract Background Persistent low peripheral oxygen saturation in children commonly prompts investigation for pulmonary or cardiovascular disease. However, when oxygen desaturation persists despite an unrevealing cardiopulmonary evaluation, dyshemoglobinemia should be considered. Case presentation We report the case of a 7-year-old girl with persistent low peripheral oxygen saturation for approximately five years. Her peripheral oxygen saturation remained between 85% and 89% on room air despite an otherwise normal clinical condition. Extensive investigations, including echocardiography, contrast echocardiography, cardiac computed tomography angiography, chest computed tomography, pulmonary function testing, and neurologic evaluation, did not identify a cardiopulmonary cause for the low oxygen saturation. Arterial blood gas analysis demonstrated a preserved partial pressure of arterial oxygen (PaO₂) of 115 mmHg on room air, increasing to 165 mmHg during a hyperoxia test. The calculated alveolar–arterial oxygen gradient was 2.3 mmHg. The discrepancy between the low pulse oximetry readings and preserved PaO₂ prompted evaluation for a dyshemoglobinemia. Co-oximetry demonstrated a methemoglobin level of 15%, supporting the diagnosis of methemoglobinemia. Conclusions Methemoglobinemia should be considered in children with persistent low peripheral oxygen saturation that is disproportionate to their clinical condition and cardiopulmonary findings. Recognition of a discrepancy between pulse oximetry and arterial oxygenation can provide an important diagnostic clue and may help prevent prolonged and unnecessary investigations.

title: ATLAS: Development and Evaluation of an AI -Enabled Framework for Anatomically Traceable Measurement Assurance in Fetal-Head Ultrasound Biometry
abstract: Abstract Background Fetal-head biometry is important for estimating gestational age, monitoring fetal development, and identifying abnormalities. As AI-enabled ultrasound systems become more prevalent, automated measurements may appear credible even with mislocalization, suboptimal imaging planes, or absent anatomical landmarks. Clinicians may receive measurements without adequate evidence on their origin or reliability. ATLAS is designed as an evidence-traceable framework to establish conditions for valid measurements. Methods ATLAS consists of a data integrity layer, Find, Confirm, and Measure. The integrity layer performs dataset-agnostic checks for image validity, label consistency, and patient-exclusive partitioning. Find localizes the fetal cranial region; Confirm verifies the anatomical structures required for valid biometry. Measure calculates biparietal diameter, occipitofrontal diameter, and head circumference using two methods: a deterministic localization geometry and a learned segmentation. Training used 3,790 eligible frames from 1,840 patients from public hospital-derived HC18/FETAL_PLANES_DB resources, with patient-exclusive training, validation, and testing; external evaluation used FP (880 frames/460 subjects) and UCL (55/15) cohorts. Outcomes were localization, CSP/LV evidence, and biometric error. Performance measures included availability/IoU, F1, mean absolute error, signed error, and prespecified joint BPD/HC tolerance. Site-specific adaptation and data-free parameter aggregation were added as secondary technical analyses for future edge deployment. Results Under controlled data-fault tests, the data integrity layer detected every introduced defect. Internal validation demonstrated that Find localized all frames (mean IoU 0.962); Confirm F1 was 0.894 for CSP and 0.819 for LV. Deterministic geometry met both biometric tolerances in 91.6% frames versus 84.1% for segmentation, reducing BPD MAE by 0.291 mm (95% CI 0.225–0.355) and improving joint-tolerance performance by 7.5pp (95% CI 5.2–9.9), meaning measurements following positive Confirm being more accurate. Externally, Find localized 99.9% (FP) and 100% (UCL) of frames, with deterministic geometry measurement performing better on FP (91.2%) and segmentation on UCL (79.6%). Site-specific adaptation improved localization but reduced biometry accuracy, which aggregation partially restored. The most memory-intensive ATLAS pathway required 16.50 MB and 57.32 ms per frame. Conclusions This study presents a compact, evidence-traceable framework that treats operationalizing selected ISUOG-relevant anatomical and biometric requirements as computational quality-control states. The system achieves performance comparable to existing approaches, while prioritizing measurement validity and transparency as core design principles. These findings underscore the necessity for clinical AI systems to provide not only accurate results but also interpretable and auditable evidence to support trustworthy integration.

title: Methodology of a prospective, single-arm, multicenter, physician-initiated study to assess the long-term safety and efficacy of the Restorer stent system for the treatment of aorto-iliac lesions. BARISTA trial.
abstract: Abstract Background Evidence regarding optimal stent selection in endovascular treatment of aorto-iliac lesions remains inconclusive, particularly in complex TASC C and D disease. Interpretation of existing data is complicated by study heterogeneity and selection bias. Both bare metal stents (BMS) and covered stents (CS) are widely used, yet comparative evidence remains limited. The BARISTA trial aims to prospectively evaluate the safety and efficacy of the Restorer iliac stent system (iVascular) and to compare its outcomes with those reported in contemporary studies assessing covered stents. Methods Between July 2022 and June 2024, this prospective multicenter study enrolled 200 patients across 14 Belgian centers. The objective is to assess two-year safety and efficacy outcomes of the Restorer iliac stent system in symptomatic aorto-iliac disease. The primary composite endpoint includes: (1) freedom from target lesion revascularization (TLR), (2) freedom from major amputation, and (3) absence of restenosis within 12 months. TLR is defined as any repeat intervention within the treated segment, including 5 mm proximal and distal to the lesion. Restenosis is defined as > 50% stenosis on duplex ultrasound with a systolic velocity ratio > 2.4. Discussion By analyzing outcomes in a large prospective cohort and comparing results with contemporary CS data, the BARISTA trial aims to support evidence-based stent selection in aorto-iliac disease. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT05293002 (2022-03-23)

title: A Study on the Application of Multimodal MRI Deep Learning in the Early Detection of Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head
abstract: Abstract Objective: Osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) is a debilitating disorder that frequently leads to hip joint dysfunction. Early and accurate diagnosis is crucial to improving clinical outcomes. This study aimed to develop a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based detection model using the You Only Look Once (YOLO) deep learning framework for automatic identification of early-stage ONFH, and to systematically evaluate how different MRI modalities affect detection performance and their potential for clinical decision support. Methods: We retrospectively collected MRI data from 253 ONFH patients across two medical centers, including T1-weighted Imaging (T1WI) and T2-weighted Imaging (T2WI) sequences. After standardized preprocessing, the dataset was partitioned into training, validation, and test sets (7:1:2). Two sequential experiments were conducted. Experiment 1 compared six YOLO generations (v3, v5, v8, v10, v11, v13) using single-center T1WI data, with precision (P), recall (R), mean average precision (mAP), and inference speed as primary metrics. Experiment 2 applied the optimal model to single-modality (T1WI or T2WI) and multimodal fused images from both centers, using the same metrics to quantify detection efficacy and validate multicenter robustness. Results: In Experiment 1, YOLO v11 outperformed all other models, achieving a mAP@0.5 of 0.966, a recall of 0.941, and a per-frame inference time of 4.9 ms. In Experiment 2, the multimodal fusion input (T1WI+T2WI) yielded the highest performance across all modalities, with a mAP@0.5 of 0.9637, a recall of 0.9388, and the fastest inference time (3.0 ms), surpassing both T1WI (R=0.9159, 4.9 ms) and T2WI (R=0.9113, 6.0 ms) alone. Conclusion: The proposed YOLO v11 model demonstrates excellent performance in MRI-based ONFH detection, and the multimodal fusion strategy further improves both diagnostic accuracy and computational efficiency. This approach addresses the dual clinical requirements for high precision and real-time processing, offering a practical and objective intelligent tool for early ONFH screening.

title: Material selection for a 3D-printed tissue-equivalent cost-effective phantom for radiotherapy quality assurance
abstract: Abstract Background and Aims: Patient-specific 3D-printed phantoms are increasingly used for radiotherapy quality assurance (QA) because they are cost-effective and reproduce individual patient anatomy. A major challenge is identifying materials that mimic human tissue.In this work we systematically evaluate radiological properties of various commonly available and industrial 3D printing materials, whereby we include a combined characterization at diagnostic (keV) and therapeutic (MeV) photon energies. Methods and Materials: Over 60 cubes of plastic samples of about 30 materials and different in-fill densities were printed using three different filament printers. CT scans were acquired and the average Hounsfield Units (HU) for each sample was determined. Massdensities (ρm), electron density (ρe), and relative electron density (RED) were assessed. All samples were compared with ICRU reference data. The response at therapeutic energies was evaluated by irradiating the samples and measuring the deposited dose using a micro-diamond detector. These were compared with Pinnacle TPS predictions. Results: The tested materials with 100% filling showed HU values between -95.52 and 238.63. The ρm, ρe, and RED values ranged from 0.963 to 1.228 g/cm3, 3.128 to 3.898 ×1023 and 0.935 to 1.166, respectively. Deviations between measured and TPS dose ranged from -1.34% to 1.36%. Several materials matched ICRU soft-tissue specification. By varying the in-fill density of the materials, refinements could be realized. Conclusions: By combining CT-based characterization with MeV dosimetric validation and testing materials from multiple printing technologies, we identified several candidate plastics suitable for soft-tissue-equivalent radiotherapy phantoms. These can be printed using moderately priced 3D printers (<∼5k euro).

title: Associations of initial blood gas parameters with post-cooling MRI-derived brain volumes and Rutherford injury scores in neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy: a retrospective exploratory study
abstract: Abstract Background Quantitative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) may reveal structural alterations not captured by conventional visual assessment in neonatal hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE). This study investigated associations between initial blood gas parameters and post-cooling MRI-derived brain volumes and Rutherford MRI injury scores in neonates treated with therapeutic hypothermia. Methods This retrospective exploratory study included 79 neonates with HIE. Initial pH, partial pressure of carbon dioxide, bicarbonate, base excess, and lactate were evaluated in relation to 50 absolute MRI-derived brain-volume measures and the consensus Rutherford score. Associations were assessed using Spearman correlations and separate multivariable linear regression models adjusted for gestational age at birth, postnatal age at MRI, and sex, with HC3 heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors. Two blinded radiologists independently assigned Rutherford scores and resolved disagreements by consensus. Secondary analyses compared neonates with pH ≤ 7.00 and pH > 7.00. The Benjamini–Hochberg procedure controlled the false discovery rate within prespecified analysis families. Results Consensus Rutherford scores were available for all 79 neonates (mean, 6.91 ± 1.34; median, 7; interquartile range, 6–8; range, 4–9). Interobserver agreement was good (absolute-agreement intraclass correlation coefficient, 0.789; quadratic-weighted κ, 0.787); exact agreement occurred in 50.6% of examinations, and scores differed by no more than 1 point in 88.6%. After false-discovery-rate correction, no initial blood gas parameter was significantly associated with the consensus Rutherford score in either unadjusted or adjusted analyses. The adjusted mean score difference between the pH groups was−0.20 (95% confidence interval,−0.93 to 0.54; p = 0.597). No blood gas–volume association remained significant after correction, and no absolute or intracranial-volume-normalized measure differed significantly between the pH groups. Conclusions This exploratory cohort provided no evidence of associations between initial blood gas parameters and post-cooling Rutherford MRI injury scores or global and regional brain volumes after correction for multiple comparisons. These findings do not exclude clinically relevant associations and require confirmation in larger studies using neonatal-validated segmentation methods.

title: Energy-Based Devices for GLP-1 Receptor Agonist-Associated Facial Aging: A Tissue-Specific Safety Framework.
abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA)-associated rapid weight loss may be accompanied by facial changes resembling accelerated aging, colloquially termed "Ozempic face". In this review, this proposed phenotype is termed GLP-1RA-associated facial accelerated aging (GLP-1RA-FAA) and is characterized primarily by facial volume loss and skin laxity, with possible but incompletely characterized alterations in dermal-adipose support, adipose-derived stem-cell biology, fibroblast-extracellular-matrix homeostasis, and facial muscle. Demand for energy-based device (EBD) treatment in this population is increasing; however, whether conventional EBD parameters are effective or safe in medication-associated facial volume depletion is unknown. A narrative review was informed by structured searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library from January 2000 through August 31, 2026. Evidence was selected for clinical directness and relevance to radiofrequency, high-intensity focused ultrasound, broadband light, microwave, extracorporeal shock wave therapy, diode laser, and synchronized radiofrequency with high-intensity facial electrical stimulation. Available modalities differ in their intended tissue depth and in the potential relevance of three conceptual targets: preservation of adipose tissue, dermal fibroblast-extracellular-matrix remodeling, and facial muscle-SMAS support. Preclinical body-contouring studies suggest that sustained subcutaneous heating in the approximate 43-45°C range can be associated with adipocyte injury or apoptosis; however, no facial thermal dose threshold has been established, particularly in GLP-1RA-treated patients. No individual EBD modality has demonstrated simultaneous restoration of adipose, dermal, and muscle-related targets in prospective GLP-1RA-specific studies. Conservative control of treatment depth, careful avoidance of unnecessary deep energy deposition in volume-depleted regions, investigation of low-intensity dermal remodeling strategies, and evaluation of muscle-targeting approaches are proposed as research considerations. These concepts are hypothesis generating and do not constitute clinical recommendations or standards of care. Prospective controlled studies in well-characterized GLP-1RA-treated populations are required before device-specific protocols can be adopted.

title: Current Applications and Emerging Horizons of Artificial Intelligence in Temporal Bone Computed Tomography.
abstract: The temporal bone has intricate anatomy. CT examinations can clearly depict fine anatomical structures and subtle lesions, providing indispensable imaging evidence for diagnosing otologic diseases and planning surgical procedures. However, image interpretation has several inherent limitations, including subjectivity, substantial interobserver variability, and heavy reliance on physician experience, all of which can compromise clinical decision-making and lead to inconsistent patient management. In recent years, AI-driven approaches have made significant progress in this field, particularly in optimizing image quality, identifying key anatomical structures, and assisting in the diagnosis of common otologic diseases. These advances span multiple tasks and have gradually narrowed the performance gap between automated tools and expert readers. Despite encouraging results in research settings, AI tools continue to encounter multiple obstacles in the transition from algorithmic validation to routine clinical use. These challenges include insufficient and imbalanced training data, limited generalizability across diverse populations and imaging protocols, and a persistent lack of clinician trust arising from the "black-box" nature of these models. Moreover, the absence of standardized benchmarks and prospective clinical trials further impedes the deployment of these technologies in routine otologic practice. This paper comprehensively reviews current AI applications in temporal bone CT imaging and discusses related emerging technologies, aiming to provide new perspectives and methods for clinical practice.

title: ECTU-Net: Efficient Channel Attention and Transformer Integration for Liver Tumor Segmentation in CT Images.
abstract: Background U-Net and its variants have demonstrated strong local feature extraction in medical image segmentation. Methods Efficient Channel Attention-Transformer U-Net (ECTU-Net) is proposed to recover fine boundaries and refine multi-scale features. A lightweight four-layer U-Net serves as the backbone. Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) modules enhance channel-wise feature selection, and compact Transformer blocks learn global dependencies. A Flatten-Transformer-Reshape process at the bottleneck replaces high-dimensional convolutions to capture pixel-level long-range dependencies. Results On LiTS17, ECTU-Net improves the Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) by 9.20% over the original U-Net and reduces FLOPs by 42.3%. The Transformer block adds only 0.09M parameters while improving global context modeling. Discussion ECTU-Net outperforms the comparison models in liver tumor segmentation and accurately delineates tumor regions. It combines high segmentation accuracy with parameter efficiency. However, the limited sample size restricts the generalizability of the findings. Conclusion ECTU-Net enables high-precision medical image segmentation in resource-constrained settings and shows strong potential for clinical application.

title: Genital Tuberculosis (GTB): Insights into Diagnosis, Treatment, Clinical Trials and Patents-A Comprehensive Review.
abstract: Genital Tuberculosis (GTB) represents a frequently unrecognized type of extrapulmonary Tuberculosis (TB) that affects the female reproductive system. The condition results in infertility, menstrual cycle disturbances, and pelvic pain. The condition is difficult to detect at an early stage because its mild symptoms can manifest in different body parts. Therefore, medical professionals require better methods for diagnosing and treating patients. This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations, diagnostic approaches, therapeutic strategies, and current advancements in the management of GTB. The study presents information on New Drug Delivery systems (NDDs), current clinical trials, and new patents to guide future research. A literature-based narrative review was conducted, focusing on peer-reviewed articles, clinical studies, patents, and recent advances in diagnostics and therapeutics of GTB. The study focused on three main areas: anatomical site-specific manifestations; laboratory instruments and drug medications. The fallopian tubes are the most commonly affected site (90-100%), followed by the endometrium (50-60%), ovaries (20-30%), cervix (5-10%), while involvement of the vagina and vulva is rare (<1%). The diagnosis of GTB becomes problematic because both its visible and hidden symptoms start to appear. The development of effective detection methods depends on both traditional diagnostic methods and modern molecular methods, which include specialized laboratory equipment, imaging techniques, and histopathology. Current clinical trials and new patent approvals demonstrate the development of new methods for diagnosing and treating GTB, including improved therapeutic approaches and drug delivery systems. GTB presents both diagnostic and treatment difficulties because patients show different symptoms that can remain hidden. The combination of methods for diagnosing and treating GTB, through improved therapeutic approaches and drug-delivery systems, will enhance detection, treatment outcomes, and the ability to maintain fertility. The research should investigate personalized medicine approaches, molecular diagnostic technologies, and new therapeutic delivery systems to address the existing clinical needs in GTB treatment.

title: Hemorrhagic lumbar synovial cyst mimicking a neoplastic process: illustrative case.
abstract: Background Synovial cysts with extensive hemorrhage, marked mass effect, and tumor-like appearance are rare and may mimic neoplastic processes. Observations A 56-year-old man presented with progressive mechanical low back pain, neurogenic claudication, gait instability, and bilateral weakness. MRI revealed a 2.0-cm lesion arising from the right L3 facet joint, causing severe central canal and right foraminal stenosis with displacement of the cauda equina. Imaging features suggested pigmented villonodular synovitis. Intraoperatively, however, the lesion appeared fleshy, partially encapsulated, and dural adherent, resembling a nerve sheath tumor, with necrotic regions suggesting malignancy. Frozen-section analysis demonstrated benign fibroconnective tissue with marked reactive and degenerative changes, including necrosis and hemosiderin deposition, without evidence of neoplasia. Intraoperative confirmation of benign pathology shifted operative priorities toward anatomical preservation rather than extent of resection; gross-total removal was nevertheless achieved and the patient had complete neurological recovery. Permanent pathology was most consistent with a degenerative synovial cyst with hemorrhage. Lessons This case highlights the importance of integrating imaging findings, intraoperative appearance, and histopathological evaluation rather than relying on a single diagnostic modality. The combination of a focused differential and confirmation of benign pathology guided the extent of resection, balancing maximal lesion removal with preservation of adjacent structural elements. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26317.

title: Spindle cell oncocytoma: illustrative case.
abstract: Background Spindle cell oncocytoma (SCO) is a rare, nonadenomatous sellar tumor that often mimics pituitary adenomas both radiographically and clinically, making diagnosis and treatment difficult. Observations A 67-year-old male presented with fatigue and weakness, with MRI revealing an enhancing sellar mass with suprasellar extension and laboratory findings consistent with panhypopituitarism. He underwent endoscopic endonasal resection, which revealed a fibrous, highly vascular tumor adherent to surrounding tissue, consistent with SCO on final pathological analysis. Gross-total resection (GTR) was achieved, and the patient has been monitored regularly with no signs of recurrence at 9 months postoperatively. Lessons SCOs are an exceedingly rare entity often indistinguishable from pituitary adenomas preoperatively, yet their intraoperative hypervascularity and fibrous texture can complicate resection and predispose patients to recurrence. Accurate identification of these tumors and GTR when possible are essential to appropriate treatment. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26333.

title: Endoscopic transorbital approach for resection of Meckel's cave aspergillosis: illustrative case.
abstract: Background Aspergillosis involving Meckel's cave (MC) is rare. Only 5 previous case reports exist in the literature. The primary treatment for this disease is surgical debridement combined with antifungal therapy. The authors present a minimally invasive technique using an endoscopic transorbital approach (ETOA) to manage this condition. Observations A 26-year-old male corn farmer presented with progressive right-sided facial pain and numbness for 1 month. MRI demonstrated a markedly hypointense T2 signal lesion in the right MC with gadolinium enhancement. CT revealed sphenoid sinus opacification with bony erosion. Nasal endoscopy with sphenoidotomy and mucosal biopsy were noncontributory. He underwent an ETOA via lateral canthotomy. Irregular yellowish rubbery tissue adherent to all divisions of the trigeminal nerve was resected. Histopathological analysis confirmed septate fungal hyphae. The fungal culture identified Aspergillus flavus. After 6 months of voriconazole, the facial pain resolved despite persistent numbness, and MRI demonstrated radiological resolution of the lesion. The patient remained free of recurrence at 1 year. Lessons MC aspergillosis can present as trigeminal neuropathy in immunocompetent patients. The ETOA provides direct extradural access permitting tissue diagnosis and debridement without temporal lobe retraction. Combined with antifungal therapy, this approach may be a feasible strategy for this disease. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26736.

title: Postoperative epidural fluid collection mimicking epidural abscess: illustrative cases.
abstract: Background After craniotomy, fluid may accumulate in the surgical bed, raising suspicion for hemorrhage, abscess, or postoperative pseudomeningocele. Typically, peripheral contrast enhancement, internal restricted diffusion, and adjacent edema are consistent with infection. Observations The authors present 4 cases with postoperative epidural fluid collections mimicking epidural abscesses on MRI with restricted diffusion on diffusion-weighted imaging. Three of these cases were associated with adjacent brain edema. The fluid appeared 1-3 months after the surgery on routine follow-up MRI in the absence of clinical symptoms, and nearly resolved, either spontaneously without treatment or with conservative therapy alone. Given imaging findings concerning for infection in the absence of symptoms, diagnosis and management were challenging. Lessons When there is increased epidural fluid collection after craniotomy, radiographic findings may mimic abscess, but they are not always clinically significant. Clinical assessment is a crucial component of the diagnosis to avoid unnecessary intervention, and follow-up imaging is recommended. The pathogenesis of this restricting, enhancing fluid collection remains unclear. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26757.

title: Proliferative Sarcoid Retinopathy With Bilateral Tractional Retinal Detachment.
abstract: A 28-year-old male patient without previously diagnosed systemic disease or any ocular history presented with 3 months of progressive blurred vision in both eyes. His ocular exam revealed bilateral vitreous hemorrhage, tractional retinal detachments (TRDs), and extensive retinal neovascularization (NV). His systemic workup revealed elevated angiotensin-converting enzyme, bilateral hilar, and mediastinal adenopathy on computed tomography (CT) chest scan, and extensive multifocal leptomeningeal-enhancing nodules within the posterior fossa on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) brain scan, confirming sarcoidosis with neurologic and ocular involvement. Ocular complications of sarcoidosis predominantly involve the anterior segment, with anterior uveitis as the most common presentation overall. While posterior findings of ocular sarcoidosis are less common, these include but are not limited to retinal periphlebitis with candlewax drippings, choroidal granulomas, and optic nerve involvement, with cystoid macular edema representing the leading cause of vision loss. This report presents a unique case of bilateral TRDs and retinal NV as the initial manifestation of sarcoidosis. Improved awareness of atypical ocular presentations of sarcoidosis is critical for facilitating earlier diagnosis and timely intervention.

title: Changes in Macular Area Following Epiretinal Membrane Removal and Its Correlation With Anatomical and Functional Parameters.
abstract: Background and objective This study aimed to evaluate changes in macular area after pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) with epiretinal membrane (ERM) peeling and determine correlations with visual acuity (VA) and optical coherence tomography (OCT)-based anatomical parameters. Patients and methods This retrospective study included 29 eyes with idiopathic ERM undergoing PPV and membrane peeling. Macular area was quantified using infrared images at baseline and 7 to 9 days, and 30 days and 3 months postoperatively. OCT parameters-including central macular thickness (CMT), inner retinal thickness (IRT), macular volume, disorganization of retinal inner layers (DRIL), and ellipsoid zone (EZ) status-were analyzed. Correlations between macular area change, VA (logMAR), and OCT parameters were assessed. Results Macular area significantly increased from 37.59 ± 11.67 mm 2 to 42.77 ± 10.92 mm 3 at 3 months ( P < .001). VA improved from 0.48 ± 0.19 to 0.20 ± 0.17 ( P < .001). CMT decreased from 508.68 ± 74.01 µm to 395.03 ± 63.62 µm ( P < .001). DRIL decreased from 82.8% to 31%. EZ disruption decreased from 37.9% to 17.2%; however, this change did not reach statistical significance (exact McNemar P = .070). Macular area change was not significantly correlated with visual acuity improvement at 3 months ( r = 0.081, P = .758), although macular area at 3 months was negatively correlated with CMT ( r = -0.560, P = .016). Conclusion Macular area expansion after ERM peeling appears to reflect structural recovery following release of retinal traction. Although some associations with visual outcomes were observed, independent prognostic value remains uncertain and requires confirmation in larger prospective studies.

title: Prediction of Acute Kidney Injury with Venous Excess Ultrasound (VExUS) Scoring Versus Renal Resistive Index (RRI) in Patients Undergoing On-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Prospective Observational Study.
abstract: Background The diagnosis of acute kidney injury (AKI) using conventional markers such as serum creatinine and urine output is often delayed, prompting interest in bedside ultrasound-based predictors. This study compared renal resistive index (RRI) and venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) scoring for early prediction of AKI after on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Methods In this prospective observational study, 180 adult patients were enrolled. RRI and VExUS assessments were performed preoperatively and within 3 hours of cardiothoracic ICU admission. AKI was diagnosed within 48 hours postoperatively using kidney disease: improving global outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were constructed for RRI and VExUS parameters, and diagnostic accuracy was assessed using area under ROC curve (AUROC), sensitivity, and specificity. Results AKI occurred in 48 patients (26.7%). Postoperative RRI showed excellent discrimination for AKI (AUROC 0.854; cut-off ≥0.68: sensitivity 75%, specificity 86%, negative predictive value [NPV] 90.5%), outperforming preoperative RRI (AUROC 0.681). VExUS showed limited predictive performance (preoperative AUROC 0.588; postoperative AUROC 0.623). The baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in the AKI group was significantly lower than in the patients who did not develop AKI [70.3 ml/min/1.73 m2 vs 79.4 ml/min/1.73 m2]. Diabetes mellitus was more common in the AKI group (62.5% vs 35.6%, P = 0.002). Postoperative urine output remained significantly lower in AKI patients on day 1 and day 2 (P < 0.001). Conclusion Postoperative RRI ≥ 0.68 demonstrated the best predictive performance for early AKI in our cohort, outperforming preoperative RRI, ΔRRI or change in RRI, and VExUS scores, supporting the predominant role of intrarenal arterial hemodynamic alterations in early postoperative renal injury.

title: Robotic Parenchyma-Preserving Pancreatic Resection for Focal Congenital Hyperinsulinism in an Infant.
abstract: Background Robot-assisted surgery has been increasingly adopted over traditional laparoscopic and open procedures. However, its application in neonates and infants remains limited. Restricted space, delicate tissues, and the need for special instruments complicate its use. This case report describes the application of robot-assisted surgery in an infant with focal congenital hyperinsulinism. Materials and methods We describe the management of focal congenital hyperinsulinism in an infant using robotic surgery with indocyanine green injection, intraoperative ultrasound, and a suture-based retraction technique. Case description Herein, we present a case of an infant weighing less than 5 kg who underwent robotic surgery. The procedure was performed using the 3 arms of the da Vinci Xi robotic system and a suture-based intraoperative retraction technique. Intraoperative frozen sections confirmed the complete excision of the focal disease. Final histopathology revealed focal adenomatous hyperplasia. Intraoperatively, plasma glucose levels transiently increased after resection peaking at 23.1 mmol/L. Intravenous dextrose was discontinued. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the infant was discharged on postoperative day nine after tolerating full oral feeds. At follow-up in 8 months, the child remained euglycemic without any medical therapy or hypoglycemic episodes. Discussion This case demonstrates the feasibility of robotic-assisted parenchyma-preserving pancreatic resection in a 4.6-kg infant. Careful attention to operative planning and the use of adjuncts, such as indocyanine green fluorescence and intraoperative ultrasonography, is critical. Minimizing the number of additional ports and using suture-based retraction techniques can help achieve successful robotic surgery in this high-risk population.

title: Deep Learning Trained Without Target-Domain Labels Improves Risk Stratification Over Expert Coronary Calcium Reading on Routine Attenuation Correction CT
abstract: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) is an established measure of coronary atherosclerosis on computed tomography (CT). Many SPECT and most PET myocardial perfusion studies already include a low-dose CT scan from which coronary calcium could be reported, yet it almost never is. CAC may not be reported due to image noise, cardiac motion, or the absence of a reliable reference standard. Deep learning (DL) models trained on these low-dose CT scans inherit the same uncertainty, because their reference labels are drawn on the degraded images. We bypassed this limitation by training a DL CAC model entirely outside the target domain: expert labels from high-quality gated CT were inherited by synthetic ungated images derived from those same scans, so that no CTAC scan was annotated, and no real CTAC image was used, at any point in training. Models were trained using one center and externally tested in two other centers. Because each synthetic image is derived from the gated scan itself, expert gated segmentations remain valid voxel-for-voxel without registration. Using these pairs, we developed a cross-domain knowledge adaptation model (knowledge adaptation, KAD-CAC). The DL models were externally tested on 5969 patients with a median age of 64 (IQR 56 - 73), of whom 50.2% were male. The KAD-CAC model had higher Cohens kappa K (0.86, 95% CI 0.84 - 0.88) compared to a convolutional LSTM model (K 0.78, 95% CI 0.76 - 0.80, p<0.01), or models trained with only gated images (K 0.81, 95% CI 0.80 - 0.82, p<0.01). Net reclassification improvement for death or myocardial infarction over a clinical and perfusion baseline was greatest for the KAD-CAC model and exceeded that of expert CAC reading on the same CTAC scans (difference 0.089, 95% CI 0.051 to 0.125, p<0.001). A model trained without any labels from CTAC scans therefore stratified risk of death or MI better than expert reading of the same scans. Patients classified as CAC 0 by KAD-CAC had lower adjusted risk of death or MI than patients classified as CAC 0 by experts (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.25 - 0.98). We use paired synthetic ungated scans to transfer expert gated CAC annotations into the ungated domain, resulting in better vessel-level CAC scoring and improved risk reclassification compared with expert reading of the same scans. Automated CAC scoring could be added to every myocardial perfusion imaging report without additional imaging or radiation. The approach provides a general route to expert-quality supervision for any acquisition in which the native reference standard is unreliable.

Many SPECT and most PET myocardial perfusion studies already include a low-dose CT scan from which coronary calcium could be reported, yet it almost never is. CAC may not be reported due to image noise, cardiac motion, or the absence of a reliable reference standard. Deep learning (DL) models trained on these low-dose CT scans inherit the same uncertainty, because their reference labels are drawn on the degraded images. We bypassed this limitation by training a DL CAC model entirely outside the target domain: expert labels from high-quality gated CT were inherited by synthetic ungated images derived from those same scans, so that no CTAC scan was annotated, and no real CTAC image was used, at any point in training. Models were trained using one center and externally tested in two other centers. Because each synthetic image is derived from the gated scan itself, expert gated segmentations remain valid voxel-for-voxel without registration. Using these pairs, we developed a cross-domain knowledge adaptation model (knowledge adaptation, KAD-CAC). The DL models were externally tested on 5969 patients with a median age of 64 (IQR 56 - 73), of whom 50.2% were male. The KAD-CAC model had higher Cohens kappa K (0.86, 95% CI 0.84 - 0.88) compared to a convolutional LSTM model (K 0.78, 95% CI 0.76 - 0.80, p<0.01), or models trained with only gated images (K 0.81, 95% CI 0.80 - 0.82, p<0.01). Net reclassification improvement for death or myocardial infarction over a clinical and perfusion baseline was greatest for the KAD-CAC model and exceeded that of expert CAC reading on the same CTAC scans (difference 0.089, 95% CI 0.051 to 0.125, p<0.001). A model trained without any labels from CTAC scans therefore stratified risk of death or MI better than expert reading of the same scans. Patients classified as CAC 0 by KAD-CAC had lower adjusted risk of death or MI than patients classified as CAC 0 by experts (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.25 - 0.98). We use paired synthetic ungated scans to transfer expert gated CAC annotations into the ungated domain, resulting in better vessel-level CAC scoring and improved risk reclassification compared with expert reading of the same scans. Automated CAC scoring could be added to every myocardial perfusion imaging report without additional imaging or radiation. The approach provides a general route to expert-quality supervision for any acquisition in which the native reference standard is unreliable.

title: Ascending Aortic Calcium Identifies Patients at Risk Despite Normal Myocardial Flow, Perfusion and Coronary Calcium: A 13-Site Cohort Study
abstract: Background Patients with normal perfusion, normal myocardial flow reserve (MFR) and no coronary artery calcium (CAC) on myocardial perfusion imaging are considered low risk. Yet, adverse events still occur and no routinely reported imaging marker stratifies residual risk. This study aims to determine whether fully automated ascending aortic calcification (AAC) from the attenuation correction CT stratifies risk in these patients. Methods In the multicenter REFINE-PET registry, AAC was quantified from non-contrast CT using deep learning aortic segmentation and Agatston scoring. Triple-normal was defined as stress total perfusion deficit (TPD) <5%, MFR >2 and CAC 0. The primary endpoint was cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or heart failure admission, with heart failure admission as key secondary endpoint. Cox models were adjusted for clinical confounders. Results Of 21,923 patients, 3,580 (16.3%) were triple-normal, of whom 1,322 (36.9%) had AAC (median Agatston 65, IQR 22-212). Agreement with three blinded readers was good to excellent (Intraclass correlation coefficient 0.87-0.90). Over a median follow-up of 52 months (IQR 26-69), 194 primary events occurred. Per standard deviation, AAC was independently associated with the primary endpoint (adjusted HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.09-1.40; p<0.001), heart failure admission (adjusted HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.10-1.55; p=0.003) and all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 1.17, 95% CI 1.04-1.32; p=0.009). AAC improved model fit beyond clinical factors, MFR and TPD (p≤0.009), with modest gains in discrimination (ΔC 0.007-0.009). Conclusions In patients with normal PET readouts, automated AAC was independently associated with adverse outcomes, most strongly heart failure admission, beyond clinical risk factors, perfusion and flow. Clinical Perspective What Is New? In 3,580 patients with normal perfusion, normal myocardial flow reserve and no coronary artery calcium on PET, more than one in three had ascending aortic calcification on the attenuation correction CT. Ascending aortic calcification was independently associated with cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or heart failure admission (adjusted hazard ratio per SD 1.24, 95% CI 1.09-1.40), most strongly with heart failure admission. A fast, fully automated method scored ascending aortic calcification with agreement to expert readers similar to agreement between readers. What Are the Clinical Implications? A normal perfusion PET with normal flow and no coronary calcium does not mean uniformly low risk when the ascending aorta is calcified. Because ascending aortic calcification is scored automatically from the CT acquired with every perfusion PET, it could be reported routinely without additional scanning, cost or radiation. Patients presumed low risk who have ascending aortic calcification may warrant heart failure-oriented prevention, such as natriuretic peptide screening, pending prospective validation.
