title: A Nerve Root-Centered Classification System for Lumbar Disc Herniation: Development and Reliability Assessment
abstract: Abstract Background Existing classifications of lumbar disc herniation (LDH) mainly describe disc morphology, migration, or canal compromise, but provide limited information regarding the spatial relationship between the herniated disc and the affected nerve root. This study developed a nerve root-centered classification for patients undergoing percutaneous endoscopic lumbar discectomy (PELD) and evaluated its observer reliability and agreement with intraoperative findings. Methods This single-center retrospective classification-development and reliability study included 516 patients with LDH who underwent PELD between January and December 2022. The Peking University Third Hospital (PUTH) classification integrates the cranio-caudal origin pattern of the affected nerve root (Types 1–3) with the location of the herniated disc relative to the nerve root (Types A–D). Preliminary classifications based on preoperative magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) were compared with consensus reference classifications established through blinded review of intraoperative videos by senior spine surgeons. Intraobserver and interobserver reliability were evaluated by three surgeons from the study institution using all 516 cases and by five surgeons from external institutions using 100 proportionately stratified cases from the same cohort. Clinical outcomes were summarized descriptively after a minimum follow-up of 2 years. Results MRI-based classifications agreed with the consensus video-based reference classifications in 486 of 516 cases (94.2%). Thirty discordant cases were mainly attributable to severe nerve root compression, incomplete visualization of the nerve root origin on MRI, or anatomical variation. Internal intraobserver agreement was substantial to excellent (κ = 0.776–0.842), and internal interobserver agreement was excellent (κ = 0.837). Among external raters, intraobserver agreement was substantial (κ = 0.659–0.756), whereas interobserver agreement was also substantial but lower than that observed internally (κ = 0.645). At final follow-up, lower VAS and ODI scores and a higher JOA score were observed compared with preoperative values. Symptomatic recurrence occurred in 13 patients (2.52%), and postoperative complications occurred in 9 patients (1.74%). Conclusion The PUTH classification demonstrated substantial-to-excellent observer reliability and high MRI–operative agreement in a single-center cohort undergoing PELD. Independent prospective multicenter studies are required to determine its generalizability and influence on surgical decision-making and clinical outcomes.

title: Snowman-like appearance in spinal capillary hemangioma with combined intra- and extramedullary components: two case reports
abstract: Abstract Background Capillary hemangiomas are benign tumors primarily found in the soft tissues of the head and neck, and their occurrence in the spinal cord is rare. Because of its rarity and nonspecific radiological features, it is often difficult to differentiate from more common intradural-extramedullary tumors. Case presentation: We report two cases of thoracic spinal capillary hemangioma with intra- and extramedullary components. MRI demonstrated strongly and homogeneously enhancing tumors with a snowman-like appearance. Intraoperatively, both tumors were highly vascular, with contiguous intra- and extramedullary components closely associated with the spinal pia mater. The tumors were resected en bloc after control of tumor-related vessels. Histopathological examination demonstrated proliferation of capillary-sized vessels without stromal cells, consistent with capillary hemangioma. Postoperative recovery was uneventful. Conclusion A snowman-like appearance is not necessarily specific to spinal hemangioblastoma and may also occur in spinal capillary hemangioma with combined intra- and extramedullary components. Capillary hemangioma should therefore be considered in the differential diagnosis when this imaging pattern is observed.

title: Abrupt Onset of Crescentic IgA Nephropathy Superimposed on Glycogen Storage Disease Type Ia: A 15-Year Longitudinal Pediatric Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Renal involvement is a primary determinant of long-term morbidity in glycogen storage disease type Ia (GSD-Ia). It classically presents as non-immune-mediated metabolic nephropathy that slowly advances from asymptomatic glomerular hyperfiltration to focal segmental glomerulosclerosis. The concurrence of an immune-complex glomerulopathy is exceptionally rare. We report the first pediatric case of GSD-Ia complicated by biopsy-proven crescentic IgA nephropathy followed longitudinally over 15 years, shedding light on the diagnostic vigilance and therapeutic adaptations required for superimposed glomerulonephritis. Case presentation: A 15-year-old male with genetically confirmed GSD-Ia had a history of early glomerular hyperfiltration, recurrent nephrolithiasis, and low-grade proteinuria since age 4, remaining clinically stable for over six years on dietary management and angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors. At 11 years of age, despite well-controlled metabolic parameters, he abruptly developed nephrotic-range proteinuria (urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio: 7207.5 mg/g Cr; 24-hour urine protein: 4483.8 mg) and hematuria. Given this sharp deviation from typical metabolic nephropathy, a percutaneous renal biopsy was performed. Histopathology revealed chronic tubulointerstitial injury superimposed with crescentic IgA nephropathy featuring cellular and fibrocellular crescents in 7 of 25 glomeruli, strong mesangial IgA deposition, and confluent electron-dense deposits. Induction therapy with oral glucocorticoids and mycophenolate mofetil markedly reduced proteinuria. Due to residual proteinuria, treatment was transitioned to low-dose glucocorticoids combined with tacrolimus, which successfully achieved clinical remission. All immunosuppressants were discontinued by early 2026. At the 15-year follow-up, the patient maintained durable clinical remission with preserved renal function (serum creatinine: 31 µmol/L; urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio: 1051.3 mg/g Cr). Conclusions In patients with GSD-Ia, an abrupt onset of nephrotic-range proteinuria strongly warrants suspicion of superimposed glomerulonephritis rather than intrinsic metabolic nephropathy alone. Prompt renal biopsy is essential to establish an accurate diagnosis. Combining tight metabolic control with targeted calcineurin inhibitor-based immunosuppressive therapy represents an effective dual-track strategy to induce remission and preserve long-term renal function in this complex scenario.

title: Complicated Sigmoid Diverticular Disease Presenting as Extensive Retroperitoneal and Thigh Necrotizing Soft-Tissue Infection: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Necrotizing soft-tissue infection (NSTI) is a rare, rapidly progressive, and potentially fatal surgical emergency. Early diagnosis is challenging due to its nonspecific presentation, and prompt recognition followed by urgent imaging and surgical intervention is essential to improve outcome. Case presentation: A 57 year old woman presented with generalized weakness, poor oral intake, lower abdominal pain, and oliguria. She was hypotensive, hypoxic, and in acute kidney injury with metabolic acidosis. Non-contrast CT revealed complicated sigmoid diverticulitis with extensive extraluminal gas extending through the left retroperitoneum, psoas, pelvis, and thigh, consistent with an extensive necrotizing soft-tissue infection. Emergency laparotomy with resection of the diseased sigmoid colon, upper rectum, distal ileum, and cecum, followed by end ileostomy and colostomy, was performed along with extensive left thigh exploration and debridement. Despite initial improvement following source control and intensive care, she developed wound infection with carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae and progressive hemodynamic deterioration, ultimately dying of cardiac arrest on postoperative day 19. Conclusion This case highlights the challenges of recognizing deep necrotizing infection from an intra-abdominal source, emphasizing the importance of early imaging and surgical source control.

title: Agreement of Radiographic Parameters Between Digitally Reconstructed Radiographs from Weight-Bearing Cone-Beam CT and Whole-Spine Radiographs
abstract: Abstract Purpose Current spinal deformity diagnosis relies on whole-spine radiographs, while Weight-bearing Radiology 3D (WR3D) offers accurate, low-dose three-dimensional reconstruction in the standing position. This study aims to evaluate the potential of digitally reconstructed radiographs (DRRs) generated from WR3D images as a substitute for standard whole-spine radiographs. Methods In this retrospective comparative study of 67 patients who underwent both WR3D examination and whole-spine radiographs, DRRs were generated using segmentation and projection algorithms. Two observers independently measured coronal and sagittal radiographic parameters of the spine and pelvis on both imaging modalities, with intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) calculated. Paired samples t -tests and Bland-Altman analyses were performed, with mean absolute errors (MAEs) and Pearson correlation coefficients calculated. Results DRRs exhibited superior interobserver reliability compared to radiographs, particularly for pelvic incidence (PI, ICC = 0.95 vs. 0.70), pelvic tilt (PT, ICC = 0.98 vs. 0.83), sacral slope (SS, ICC = 0.94 vs. 0.79), and upper thoracic parameters. High agreement between the two imaging modalities was observed in measurements of all coronal parameters, cervical lordosis (C2-C7), thoracolumbar kyphosis (T10-L2), lumbar lordosis (L4-S1, L1-S1), PI, and PT ( p > 0.05), while differences were observed for other sagittal parameters ( p < 0.05). Conclusions DRR images based on WR3D show high agreement with radiographs for measuring most structural parameters. However, certain differences exist for global balance parameters and sagittal curvature parameters.

title: Feasibility and Safety of Sheath-Assisted Limited Repair for Iatrogenic Femoral Artery Pseudoaneurysm
abstract: Abstract Objective:To evaluate the technical feasibility, perioperative safety, and mid-term clinical outcomes of Sheath-Assisted Limited Repair (SALR) in anatomically suitable patients with iatrogenic femoral artery pseudoaneurysms (FAP). Methods: A retrospective cohort analysis was conducted on 10 consecutive patients with iatrogenic FAP who met strict anatomical eligibility criteria and underwent SALR at Binzhou Medical University Hospital between January 2015 and June 2025. Anatomical eligibility was defined as a localized, puncture-related lesion where the arterial defect could be temporarily sealed with an appropriately sized sheath, without involvement of the femoral bifurcation. The primary endpoints were technical success rate, conversion to standard open repair (SOR), reoperation/reintervention, pseudoaneurysm recurrence, and wound-related complications (infection, lymphorrhea). Secondary endpoints included operative time, intraoperative blood loss, bed rest duration, length of stay, and 24-hour postoperative VAS pain scores. Data from 30 patients undergoing SOR were documented for comparative clinical benchmarking. Results: The primary endpoints demonstrated remarkable success in the SALR cohort: the technical success rate was 100% (10/10), with no intraoperative conversions to SOR (0%), zero reinterventions or reoperations, and no recurrence of pseudoaneurysm during a mean follow-up of 24 months. No wound infections or lymphatic leaks occurred (0%). Regarding secondary endpoints, the operative time was 40.5 ± 12.5 min, median intraoperative blood loss was 20 (10, 40) mL, postoperative bed rest was 8.5 ± 2.5 h, and median hospital stay was 3.0 (2.0, 4.0) days. The 24-hour postoperative VAS score was 1.58 ± 0.9. Postoperative ultrasound confirmed 100% patency of the treated arterial segment without stenosis. Conclusion: SALR is a safe, highly feasible, and minimally invasive technique for anatomically suitable iatrogenic FAP. By utilizing the vascular sheath for in situ temporary hemostasis, it completely eliminates the need for extensive vascular dissection and proximal/distal clamping, thereby achieving high technical success, preventing lymphorrhea, and markedly accelerating postoperative recovery.

No wound infections or lymphatic leaks occurred (0%). Regarding secondary endpoints, the operative time was 40.5 ± 12.5 min, median intraoperative blood loss was 20 (10, 40) mL, postoperative bed rest was 8.5 ± 2.5 h, and median hospital stay was 3.0 (2.0, 4.0) days. The 24-hour postoperative VAS score was 1.58 ± 0.9. Postoperative ultrasound confirmed 100% patency of the treated arterial segment without stenosis.

Conclusion:

SALR is a safe, highly feasible, and minimally invasive technique for anatomically suitable iatrogenic FAP. By utilizing the vascular sheath for in situ temporary hemostasis, it completely eliminates the need for extensive vascular dissection and proximal/distal clamping, thereby achieving high technical success, preventing lymphorrhea, and markedly accelerating postoperative recovery.

title: Probable neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease in an Asian woman without detectable NOTCH2NLC repeat expansion on routine testing
abstract: Abstract Background: Neuronal intranuclear inclusion disease (NIID) is a clinically heterogeneous neurodegenerative disorder characterized by eosinophilic intranuclear inclusions. GGC repeat expansion in NOTCH2NLC is strongly associated with adult-onset NIID in East Asian populations. Fragile X-associated tremor/ataxia syndrome (FXTAS), associated with an FMR1 CGG premutation, can overlap with NIID clinically, radiologically, and pathologically. Negative targeted repeat-expansion results therefore require interpretation alongside clinicopathological findings. Case presentation: A 67-year-old Asian woman with no known family history of neurological disease developed progressive cognitive decline in 2021, followed by limb ataxia and bilateral lower-limb weakness. In 2025, her ADL and mRS scores were 51/56 and 3; MoCA and MMSE scores were 8/30 and 19/30. Electrophysiological findings suggested predominantly motor demyelinating polyneuropathy. Brain MRI showed bilateral corticomedullary-junction hyperintensities on DWI and confluent periventricular and deep white-matter abnormalities on FLAIR and T2WI. A skin biopsy obtained above the lateral malleolus showed eosinophilic intranuclear inclusions in sweat gland epithelial cells and fibroblasts, with positive SQSTM1/p62 and SUMO1 immunostaining. RP-PCR did not detect a NOTCH2NLC GGC repeat expansion. Both FMR1 alleles were reported to contain 29 CGG repeats, below the premutation range. During 14 months of follow-up, no impaired consciousness, seizures, or encephalopathy-like episodes occurred, and the mRS Scale score remained 3. Cognitive scores changed in opposite directions, precluding conclusions about cognitive change or treatment response. The clinical, radiological, and previously reported pathological findings supported probable NIID, apparently sporadic, without molecular confirmation. Conclusions: Characteristic MRI and skin biopsy findings remain diagnostically informative when routine NOTCH2NLC screening detects no expansion. FMR1 analysis aids differentiation from FXTAS. A negative targeted result alone should neither exclude NIID nor imply a novel causative gene; confirmation using an independent repeat-expansion assay or long-read sequencing should be considered when available.

title: Outcomes of Repeat Stereotactic Radiosurgery for Locally Recurrent Brain Metastases Following Initial Stereotactic Radiosurgery
abstract: Abstract Background Local recurrence after stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS1) for brain metastases remains a therapeutic challenge, and optimal re-irradiation parameters are not well defined. This study evaluated local control (LC) and predictors of radiation necrosis (RN) following repeat stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS2) for previously irradiated brain metastases. Methods This retrospective study included patients treated with SRS2 for locally recurrent brain metastases after prior SRS1. Patients who had received whole-brain radiotherapy were excluded. Follow-up MRI scans were reviewed for LC and RN according to RANO criteria. Kaplan–Meier analysis was used for LC and RN-free survival. Cox regression analysis identified predictive factors. ROC curve analysis determined optimal dosimetric cut-off values. Results Forty patients with 59 locally recurrent brain metastases treated with SRS2 to the same lesion were analyzed. Median follow-up was 11 months (range, 2–83). Median SRS2 prescription dose was 24 Gy (range, 14–35) delivered in a median of 3 fractions (range, 1–5), and median GTV diameter was 2.1 cm (range, 0.3–7.6). One-year local progression-free survival was 57.5% while one-year RN-free survival was 80%. Higher SRS2 EQD 2 (10) (> 33.6 Gy; 63.8% vs 93.1%, p = 0.007), cumulative EQD 2 (10) (> 75 Gy; 63.2% vs 91.4%, p = 0.006), SRS2 BED 10 (> 83.7 Gy; 65.8% vs 90.9%, p = 0.013), and cumulative BED 10 (> 177 Gy; 65.2% vs 91.0%, p = 0.013) were associated with significantly increased RN risk without corresponding LC benefit. Age, sex, histology, location, prior surgery, GTV and PTV diameter and volume, SRS1–SRS2 interval, dosimetric indices, and systemic therapy were not significantly associated with LC or RN. Conclusions Repeat SRS is an effective and well-tolerated salvage treatment for locally recurrent brain metastases. Doses below the identified BED and EQD 2 thresholds were associated with a lower risk of RN without significantly compromising local control. Prospective studies are warranted to validate optimal re-SRS dose constraints and treatment strategies for recurrent brain metastases.

title: Pressure is not flow: Rethinking blood pressure as a surrogate for cerebral blood flow during general anesthesia
abstract: Background Mean arterial pressure (MAP) is pharmacologically augmented in selected perioperative and critical care settings, including acute neurological conditions and after cardiac arrest, with the aim of improving cerebral perfusion, although it remains uncertain whether higher arterial pressure translates into increased cerebral blood flow (CBF). We investigated the CBF response to MAP augmentation with norepinephrine (NE), a commonly used vasopressor in perioperative and critical care settings, during propofol-based general anesthesia. Methods In this prospective within-subject interventional study, 16 neurologically intact patients with ASA physical status I–II undergoing elective surgery were studied using phase-contrast magnetic resonance imaging. CBF was quantified in the awake state and during propofol-based general anesthesia before and after NE-induced MAP augmentation. During general anesthesia, NE was titrated to increase MAP by approximately 25% from baseline. Concurrent systemic hemodynamics were assessed. Results General anesthesia was associated with a 50.1% (interquartile range, 42.1–55.7%) reduction in CBF and a 24.2% (20.3–29.2%) reduction in MAP compared with the awake state (both P<0.001). During general anesthesia, NE-induced MAP augmentation increased MAP by 25.7% (21.9–32.0%; P<0.001), whereas CBF remained unchanged (P=1.000). Cardiac output remained unchanged (P=0.163), whereas systemic vascular resistance index and cerebrovascular resistance increased by 40.0% (28.7–45.2%) and 36.2% (17.7–42.8%), respectively (both P<0.001). Changes in CBF during MAP augmentation were not associated with concurrent changes in MAP, cardiac output, or systemic vascular resistance index. Conclusions In neurologically intact patients undergoing propofol-based general anesthesia, clinically relevant NE-induced MAP augmentation did not increase CBF despite an approximately 50% lower CBF than in the awake state. These findings challenge the assumption that pharmacological elevation of an otherwise adequate MAP improves cerebral perfusion in this setting. While maintaining adequate arterial pressure remains essential, further MAP augmentation should not be assumed to increase CBF. Clinical Trial Registration: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06855407 ; NCT06855407 . Clinical Perspective What Is New? Norepinephrine-induced augmentation of mean arterial pressure by approximately 26% during propofol-based general anesthesia did not increase cerebral blood flow in neurologically intact patients. Cerebral blood flow was approximately 50% lower during general anesthesia than in the awake state and remained at this lower level during mean arterial pressure augmentation. Cardiac output remained unchanged, whereas systemic and cerebrovascular resistance increased during norepinephrine-induced mean arterial pressure augmentation. What Are the Clinical Implications? Pharmacological augmentation of an otherwise adequate mean arterial pressure should not be assumed to increase cerebral blood flow during propofol-based general anesthesia. Mean arterial pressure alone may therefore be an inadequate surrogate for cerebral blood flow when setting hemodynamic targets during general anesthesia. Maintaining adequate arterial pressure remains essential, but further pharmacological pressure augmentation should be distinguished from the treatment of hypotension.

title: Multi-centre validation of MELD-graph for automated focal cortical dysplasia detection using 7T compared to paired 3T MRI
abstract: BackgroundSoftware tools can support MRI diagnosis of focal cortical dysplasias (FCDs) - subtle, surgically-treatable lesions that underlie drug-resistant focal epilepsy (DRFE). MELD-graph, a widely used open-source tool combining surface-based morphometry with a convolutional neural network, was developed using 1.5T and 3T MRI data. 7T MRI is increasingly used for lesion detection in DRFE. This study investigated whether MELD-graph is robust to domain shift at 7T. MethodsWe collated paired 3T and 7T T1-weighted MRI, and FLAIR where available, from 23 patients with FCD (6 histologically-verified, 17 identified radiologically) and 39 healthy controls at four epilepsy centres. Manual lesion labels were used as ground truth. MELD-graph was run on 3T images, on 7T images with the default pipeline, and on 7T images with adaptations for 7T MRI (SPM bias-field correction, SynthStrip skull-stripping, sub-millimetric FreeSurfer reconstruction), with and without ComBat harmonisation. FCD detection performance and surface morphometry features were compared. ResultsSensitivity for FCD detection was 65% (15/23) at 3T, 48% (11/23) for 7T default and 52% (12/23) for 7T adapted, with Combat harmonisation. Among radiologically 3T-negative patients, 2/8 were detected at 3T and 3/8 at 7T; and among histologically confirmed FCD, 3/6 at 3T and 1/6 at 7T. Specificity was significantly lower at 7T (default 39%, adapted 45%) than 3T (76%). False-positives predominantly occurred in the basal temporal lobes. ComBat harmonisation improved specificity in all conditions and largely compensated for field-strength dependent differences in surface morphometry features. Adding FLAIR at 7T increased false-positive predictions. ConclusionSensitivity is comparable but specificity of MELD-graph is lower at 7T compared to 3T. Adaptations for 7T MRI can reduce segmentation errors but do not significantly improve FCD detection, while harmonisation improves performance. The adapted pipeline is released open-source. 7T MELD-graph outputs may inform radiologist review in challenging cases but require cautious interpretation.

title: Real-World Adaptation and External Validation of Machine-Learning Impedance Spectroscopy for Immediate Postpartum Detection of Obstetric Anal Sphincter Injuries
abstract: Obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI) requires immediate postpartum recognition for primary repair. Diagnosis relies primarily on clinical examination, as endoanal ultrasound (EAUS) is rarely a bedside option. Therefore, objective diagnostic assessment is most needed during the first postpartum hours. However, it is challenging to obtain the anatomically verified data needed to develop diagnostic technologies for this clinical window. We evaluated the translation of a machine-learning-assisted impedance spectroscopy model into its intended immediate postpartum setting. The model lifecycle comprised three sequential phases: V1 development using anatomically verified data from a prospective multicenter study (N=152); V2 real-world adaptation, comprising post-market data collection, retraining (N=144) to adapt to acute physiological tissue changes, and subsequent separate evaluation (N=125); and prospective external validation of V2 in an unseen cohort (N=70). During this separate evaluation, V2 achieved 89.6% accuracy. In external validation, all examinations occurred within 4 hours of birth (94.3% within the first hour). Against subsequent EAUS, V2 achieved 86.2% sensitivity, 92.7% specificity, and 90.0% overall accuracy. The V2 model was prospectively externally validated in its intended immediate-postpartum setting, supporting ML-assisted impedance spectroscopy as an objective adjunct, and not a replacement, to clinical OASI assessment. Further validation is required to confirm generalizability.

title: SCORES (Selection of Clinical Observations for Risk Evaluation Scores): Impact of Heart Rate Selection on Simplified Geneva Score Performance in Suspected Pulmonary Embolism
abstract: Background The Simplified Geneva Score (SGS) incorporates two heart-rate thresholds. Multiple heart-rate measurements are commonly recorded during emergency department (ED) assessment. While the original SGS specifies use of mean heart rate, real-world implementation is unlikely to reflect this, and the effect of alternative heart-rate selection methods on score performance is unknown. Methods SCORES was a retrospective within-subject study of consecutive ED patients at a single urban hospital undergoing computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) for suspected pulmonary embolism (PE). Four SGS variants were calculated using the first, highest, mean, and lowest recorded pre-CTPA heart rate. Outcomes included score output, risk classification, diagnostic performance, reclassification flow, and downstream imaging utilisation. Precision estimates and comparisons were derived using empirical resampling techniques. Results 590 episodes were reviewed with 581 included for analysis. PE was confirmed in 50 cases (8.6%). Mean SGS differed significantly across all heart-rate implementations (p<0.0001). The proportion classified as high risk varied from 15% using the lowest heart rate to 40% using the highest heart rate. Reclassification across the SGS threshold was common, with 25% of episodes changing risk category unidirectionally between lowest and highest heart rate implementations. SGS(lowest HR) compared with SGS(mean HR) and SGS(highest HR) demonstrated higher specificity (87.6% vs 73.4% vs 62.1%), improved AUROC (0.744 vs 0.704 vs 0.659), and reduced downstream CTPA utilisation (818 vs 876 vs 920 scans per 100 PEs diagnosed), with no additional pulmonary emboli missed within the complete diagnostic pathway. Conclusions Heart-rate selection materially influences SGS output, risk classification, diagnostic performance, and imaging utilisation. In this retrospective cohort, use of the lowest recorded heart rate produced the most favourable overall balance of discrimination and diagnostic efficiency, supporting prospective validation.

title: A large, comprehensive labeled MRI dataset of the human lateral ventricle choroid plexus
abstract: The choroid plexus (ChP) is a highly vascularized structure located in the brain ventricles that plays important roles in multiple central nervous system functions. ChP enlargement has been implicated in many neuropsychiatric conditions such as multiple sclerosis, depression, schizophrenia, and Alzheimer’s disease. However, limitation in the accuracy of the current segmentation tools highlight the need for more reliable methods to quantify ChP volume in healthy and clinical human populations. The shape and size of the ChP vary drastically from person to person, and currently there are no large ChP datasets which allow comprehensive training of segmentation models. Here we introduce DataPlex, a collection of 700 structural MRI brain images where the lateral ventricle ChP has been manually labeled and checked by expert human raters. DataPlex is balanced and representative across a wide range of scanning parameters, demographics, and clinical profiles, and subject-level information will be available for each labeled image. DataPlex will be open source to support the creation of reliable segmentation tools for the human lateral ventricle ChP.

title: Text-Guided Medical Image Segmentation via Residual Aggregation and Dense Alignment Representations
abstract: Specifying segmentation targets with natural language provides flexible semantic conditioning for medical image segmentation. However, existing methods still struggle to reliably ground high-level textual semantics into accurate pixel-level spatial prompts, especially under low-contrast lesions, ambiguous boundaries, and visually similar anatomical contexts. In this paper, we propose RADAR (Residual Aggregation and Dense Alignment Representations), a parameter-efficient framework for text-guided medical image segmentation. RADAR explicitly decouples and synergizes the medical semantic anchoring capability of BiomedCLIP with the prompt-driven mask decoding ability of MedSAM2, while enabling low-cost task adaptation via LoRA. Specifically, Guided Residual Depth Aggregation adaptively aggregates cross-layer features under semantic guidance to alleviate delayed textual injection and deep semantic dilution. Structured Dense Representation Alignment leverages a frozen BiomedCLIP to construct crop-level target, boundary, and context anchors, improving the local discriminability of dense features and the reliability of automatic prompts. Multi-modal Prompt Generation further converts cross-modal semantic responses into composite text, point, and mask prompts for MedSAM2 decoding. However, existing methods still struggle to reliably ground high-level textual semantics into accurate pixel-level spatial prompts, especially under low-contrast lesions, ambiguous boundaries, and visually similar anatomical contexts. title: AD-GS: Anatomical Density-guided 3D Gaussian Splatting for Sparse-View Dental CBCT Reconstruction
abstract: Sparse-view Cone-Beam Computed Tomography (CBCT) reconstruction is essential for reducing radiation dose and scan effort, but remains underconstrained due to limited projection information. Recent 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)-based CBCT reconstruction methods rely on gradient-driven densification, which becomes unstable under sparse acquisition and often leads to over-smoothed structures. We propose AD-GS, an Anatomical Density-guided 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that formulates Gaussian densification as an attenuation-aware Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling process. By interpreting Gaussians as samples from an underlying anatomical attenuation distribution, AD-GS adaptively concentrates representation capacity in high-attenuation regions, enabling sharper structural boundaries under sparse projections. To further constrain reconstruction, we incorporate a semantic regularization based on zero-shot features from Segment Anything in Medical Images, enforcing multi-view consistency through semantic priors. Experiments on the ToothFairy3 dental CBCT dataset demonstrate that AD-GS achieves superior structural fidelity and boundary preservation compared with existing 3DGS-based approaches under sparse-view settings within the dental and maxillofacial setting. Code is available at https://github.com/yulinjiaxue/AD-GS-BMVC2026.

title: GaborFlow: Hardware-Software Co-Optimization of Gabor Filter Accelerator Design
abstract: Brain tumor classification from MRI scans represents a critical challenge in medical imaging, where accuracy directly impacts patient outcomes. This paper introduces GaborFlow, a novel hardware-software co-optimization framework that revolutionizes the design of the Gabor Filter accelerator for generating feature maps to enhance brain tumor detection. Unlike conventional approaches that rely on fixed filter parameters, our method employs trainable Gabor coefficients within a carefully optimized range, integrated with an EfficientNet-B0 backbone CNN architecture. The innovation lies in the synergistic combination of software optimization through Bayesian hyperparameter tuning and hardware efficiency through precision-optimized multipliers. Our GF baseline accelerator achieves remarkable results, with 98.6% classification accuracy, 28.08% power benefits, and 48.83% footprint savings compared to state-of-the-art implementations, demonstrating that medical AI can be both highly accurate and energy-efficient. The hardware design files are made freely available for easy adoption and further usage by the researchers and designers.

title: Deep Learning-based Semantic Segmentation of Dental Radiographs: Comparative Evaluation of PSPNet, DeepLabv3, UNet, and UNet++
abstract: Accurate and efficient analysis of dental radiographs has become increasingly important for disease diagnosis and clinical decision making. In particular, dental radiographs segmentation plays a critical role as it is challenging due to several reasons, such as low contrast, noise in the images, variations in the image quality, etc. Previous studies have primarily addressed these challenges using convolutional neural networks (CNN)-based models. However, direct comparison of these segmentation models is still challenging due to the variations among the experimental settings. Therefore, we mainly compared four segmentation models, including Pyramid Scene Parsing Network (PSPNet), DeepLabV3, UNet, and UNet++, through a fair, controlled experimentation setting under varying conditions such as image sizes and batch sizes. For this, we used 1269 dental radiography images, and prior to training, we implemented a series of preprocessing techniques. To assess the models, we used several metrics, including Dice coefficient (DICE), Intersection over Union (IoU), accuracy, precision, training and validation losses. According to our results, UNet++ demonstrated the highest IoU score of 0.6719, and a DICE value of 0.7869, showing superior results in terms of segmentation, specifically when configured with an image size of 300x300 and a batch size of 16. In addition, we also explored the effect of image resolutions and batch sizes on model performance and accuracy under different architectures. Therefore, this study provides insights into the strengths of different segmentation models and the potential of deep learning-based semantic segmentation methods for improving automated dental radiograph analysis.

title: BrainAid: Efficient Brain Tumor Detection Using Lightweight CNNs and Explainable AI for Resource-Constrained Environments
abstract: A brain tumor is an unusual growth of cells in the brain that can be cancerous or not, affecting normal brain function and causing serious risk to health. Existing solutions for brain tumor classification, such as expert manual evaluations of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans, are generally inconsistent as different professionals have different criteria and can be resource-intensive, leading to delayed diagnoses. Additionally, while deep learning models have demonstrated potential, they typically require significant computational resources, motivating the need for more efficient and accessible diagnostic tools that can be deployed in real-time healthcare settings. To address these limitations, this study presents BrainAid, which makes efficient use of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Vision Transformers (ViTs) for effective classification of four-class classification of glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumor, and no-tumor MRI scans, outperforming all the standard models such as VGG16, Inception-V3, ResNet-50 and so, while integrating Explainable AI (XAI) to improve interpretability. The BrainAid is trained to classify tumors with a high precision of 98%, achieving an F1 score of 98% and an accuracy of 98% using publicly available dataset. The model is deployed on a Raspberry Pi, demonstrating efficiency in low-resource environments. This system shows the feasibility of real-time, edge-based tumor classification, providing quick diagnostic support for medical professionals and enhancing patient care in resource-limited healthcare facilities and underserved areas.

title: Generative Quantum Machine Learning Methods for Cancer Detection using Augmented Datasets
abstract: Cancer detection using AI methods and image databases faces several challenges, including limited and imbalanced image datasets, long algorithm training times, and high-complexity feature generation. In particular, many cancer image datasets contain very few malignant examples compared to benign ones, limiting the amount of minority-class data available for training. Although classical AI and especially deep learning methods have had some success in providing cancer diagnostics, Quantum Machine Learning (QML) methods may offer advantages through high-dimensional feature representations, generative data augmentation, and the exploitation of feature correlations through quantum properties such as entanglement. In this paper, we propose using a generative QML method on the compressed breast ultrasound image dataset (BUSI) to generate synthetic images and hence augmented datasets for classifier training. In particular, we train a convolutional neural network with real, synthetic, and a combination of real and synthetic images. We test the algorithm on real images and provide comparative results for all three training cases. Our results show that the classifier trained entirely on synthetic images achieved an AUC-ROC of 0.802 (80.2%), compared with 0.760 (76.0%) for the real-data baseline.

title: Long-Term Outcomes of IDH2-Mutant Sinonasal Carcinomas Compared With IDH2-Wild Type Sinonasal Undifferentiated Carcinoma.
abstract: Background Sinonasal carcinomas are aggressive and often locally invasive at presentation, with no universally accepted treatment approach. Histopathologic IDH2-mutant status appears to be associated with improved treatment response and survival. However, the clinical significance of histopathologic classification among IDH2-mutant sinonasal carcinomas, as well as that of IDH2 mutation status within SNUC, remains unclear and long-term clinical outcome data are limited. Methods Records from a prospectively maintained skull-base database at a large, tertiary care hospital system from 1986 to 2024 were reviewed. Patients with a diagnosis of SNUC or sinonasal tumor of any histopathology positive for IDH2 R172 mutation were identified. SMARCB1-deficient, SMARCA4-deficient, NUT sinonasal carcinomas, and other small round cell mimickers were excluded. After histopathologic confirmation, 22 IDH2-mutant SNUC, 14 IDH2-mutant non-SNUC, and 8 IDH2-wildtype SNUC cases were amenable to comprehensive clinicopathologic data review. A presence of IDH2 R172 and pathogenic TP53 mutations was determined by molecular testing and/or by immunohistochemistry. Results The median age at diagnosis was 58 years and 61% of patients were male. The majority of patients presented with T4b disease (41% of IDH2-mutant SNUC; 57% of IDH2-mutant non-SNUC; 75% of IDH2-wildtype SNUC; p = 0.3). There was no significant difference in the proportion of patients presenting with orbital invasion (55% IDH2-mutant SNUC; 64% IDH2-mutant non-SNUC; 75% of IDH2-wildtype SNUC; p = 0.7) or intracranial invasion (82% IDH2-mutant SNUC; 79% IDH2-mutant non-SNUC; 75% of IDH2-wildtype SNUC; p = 0.7). On histopathology, there was no significant difference in perineural invasion and margin status between the three subgroups (p > 0.6). A greater proportion of IDH2-mutant non-SNUCs had TP53 mutations (67%) than IDH2-mutant SNUC (31%) and IDH2-wildtype SNUC (29%) (p = 0.13). Across the cohort, 41% of patients received neoadjuvant chemotherapy, with a partial response by RECIST criteria in 94% of patients across the subgroups. Median follow-up was 28 months (IQR 11-64 months). 5-year DSS of 73% in IDH2-mutant SNUC, 75% in IDH2-mutant non-SNUC and 80% in IDH2-wildtype SNUC (p = 0.78). 5-year RFS was 53% in IDH2-mutant SNUC, 48% in IDH2-mutant non-SNUC and 43% in IDH2-wildtype SNUC (p = 0.78). Conclusion Upfront assessment of IDH2 mutation status in sinonasal carcinoma patients may be warranted to select patients for clinical trials with IDH-inhibitors. However, no significant differences in the extent of disease at presentation or response to induction chemotherapy were observed according to histopathologic classification among IDH2-mutant sinonasal carcinomas or IDH2 mutation status within SNUC. Larger series are required to determine the prognostic significance of IDH2 mutation status in sinonasal carcinoma patients.

title: CT radiomics and topology-based intratumoral heterogeneity for preoperative prediction of nuclear β-catenin expression in hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: Background Nuclear β-catenin accumulation reflects activation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but noninvasive preoperative prediction of this immunohistochemical phenotype remains incompletely established. Purpose To develop and externally validate CT radiomics and topology-based intratumoral heterogeneity (ITH) models for preoperative prediction of nuclear β-catenin expression in HCC. Materials and methods This multicenter retrospective study included 1029 patients with histopathologically confirmed HCC. Patients from two participating institutions formed the development cohort and were split into training (n=620; nuclear β-catenin-positive, 293) and internal validation (n=267; nuclear β-catenin-positive, 126) sets. Patients from an independent third institution formed the external validation cohort (n=142; nuclear β-catenin-positive, 43). Whole-tumor portal venous phase CT radiomics features and topology-based ITH features were extracted from the audited image-mask cohort. Model discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were evaluated using AUC, bootstrap 95% confidence intervals, calibration summaries, Brier scores, and decision curve analysis. Results In external validation, AUCs were 0.677 for the clinical model, 0.862 for the radiomics model, 0.857 for the ITH model, 0.831 for the core ITH model, 0.863 for the radiomics-ITH model, and 0.886 for the stacking model. Compared with radiomics alone, stacking showed a numerical ΔAUC of 0.024 (95% CI, -0.010 to 0.060; P=0.180). Conclusion CT radiomics and topology-based ITH features showed external predictive value for nuclear β-catenin expression in HCC. The stacking model had the highest external AUC, but its improvement over radiomics alone was not statistically significant. If prospectively validated, these CT-based approaches could complement tissue assessment for pretreatment biological stratification.

title: Development and validation of a preoperative CT-based radiomics nomogram for predicting postpancreatectomy acute pancreatitis after pancreatoduodenectomy.
abstract: Purpose To investigate the value of radiomics based on preoperative contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CECT) for predicting postpancreatectomy acute pancreatitis (PPAP) after pancreatoduodenectomy (PD). Methods A retrospective analysis included 104 patients who underwent PD and preoperative CECT between May 2019 and March 2025. Patients were randomly divided into training (n = 73) and test (n = 31) sets at a 7:3 ratio. PPAP was defined according to the biochemical and radiologic components of the International Study Group for Pancreatic Surgery (ISGPS) criteria. After pancreatic parenchyma delineation, radiomics feature extraction and selection, an optimal model was developed on the training set to calculate the radiomics score (rad-score). Independent clinical and morphological features were selected by univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses. Conventional quantitative CT attenuation ratios of the pancreatic parenchyma were also evaluated. Predictive performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Results PPAP occurred in 41 patients. Four models were compared: a clinical-morphologic model (age and main pancreatic duct [MPD] dilation), a conventional model (age, MPD dilation and arterial-to-portal ratio [A/P]), a radiomics model (rad-score alone), and a radiomics-integrated model (age, MPD dilation and rad-score). The radiomics-integrated model achieved the highest area under the curve (AUC) among the four models, with the AUC of 0.854 (95% CI 0.758-0.951) in the training set and 0.862 (95% CI 0.732-0.993) in the test set. Conclusion The radiomics-integrated model demonstrated promising performance for preoperative prediction of PPAP after PD, which may facilitate individualized risk stratification and perioperative management.

title: Interpreting ocular age estimates: source, output, evidence, and clinical meaning.
abstract: Ocular age estimates derived from fundus photographs, optical coherence tomography, ocular fluids, systemic omics, and multimodal models are increasingly reported in years. The eye is unusually tractable for organ-specific aging research because it is paired, repeatedly imageable, locally treatable, and linked to quantitative function. The familiar scale can obscure differences in what was measured, what the model was developed to predict, which quantity is reported, and what the study design can support. Existing frameworks classify visual-aging biomarkers by biological domain and context of use. We propose an eye-specific framework organized around five declarations: proximal source; development target; reported quantity; evidence design; and intended use. Laterality, reference population, disease and treatment context, technical version, and uncertainty in the stated output remain essential annotations. A raw age gap is a cross-sectional residual, and an age-adjusted deviation requires calibration outside the outcome-analysis sample. Repeated application of a cross-sectional model does not establish an individual aging rate; longitudinal claims require repeated measurements against a longitudinal reference and change distinguishable from measurement variability. Visual-aging claims also need psychophysical, performance-based, or patient-reported validation. Differences across measurement domains must be assessed both against measurement error and against the distribution expected in the reference population. A persistent difference may support a candidate biological pattern only after technical and clinical explanations have been evaluated. Prognostic and clinical claims require separate prospective and decision-level evidence. These distinctions prevent a cross-sectional age residual from being mistaken for an aging rate, a prognostic marker, or a clinically actionable test.

title: Bone marrow adipose tissue in cardiometabolic disease: marrow niche remodeling, inflammatory hematopoiesis, and vascular pathology.
abstract: Bone marrow adipose tissue (BMAT) is increasingly recognized as a metabolically active, endocrine, and immunomodulatory component of the marrow niche rather than a passive fat depot. This narrative review synthesizes biological, imaging, epidemiological, and therapeutic evidence linking BMAT and marrow metabolic activation with cardiometabolic disease. BMAT arises from marrow stromal progenitors and exhibits depot-specific heterogeneity, endocrine activity, insulin responsiveness, and context-dependent expansion during aging, diabetes, obesity, menopause, osteoporosis, and chronic kidney disease. Mechanistically, experimental studies indicate that marrow adipocytes and adipocyte-lineage niche cells can influence hematopoiesis through metabolic and local signaling, whereas trained immunity is established primarily in HSPCs, myeloid progenitors, and monocyte/macrophage populations. Human MRI/MRS studies characterize BMAT quantity and composition, whereas 18 F-FDG PET reflects non-BMAT-specific marrow activation associated with vascular inflammation and early atherosclerosis; direct BMAT-cardiovascular evidence remains limited. Emerging population imaging and genetic analyses support BMAT as a disease-associated phenotype, particularly for osteoporosis and fractures. Interventions affecting metabolic, inflammatory, skeletal, or marrow pathways have differing degrees of BMAT-related evidence, and none has established that modifying BMAT improves cardiovascular outcomes. This review identifies BMAT as an emerging research phenotype while emphasizing that its causal, prognostic, and therapeutic relevance to cardiovascular disease remains unresolved.

title: Elderly-onset rheumatoid arthritis versus polymyalgia rheumatica: A systematic review and meta-analysis on pathophysiology, diagnosis and clinical progression.
abstract: Elderly-onset rheumatoid arthritis (EORA) and polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) are among the most frequent inflammatory rheumatic diseases in patients over 50, yet their clinical differentiation, particularly when EORA presents with polymyalgic onset, poses a common diagnostic challenge. This systematic review aimed to identify the pathophysiological, clinical, imaging and treatment-response features that distinguish EORA from PMR. MEDLINE, CENTRAL and Scopus (inception to January 2026), with supplementary searches of LILACS, Google Scholar and trial registries (June 2026) were searched, including studies that compared EORA with PMR or reported separately extractable data for both; risk of bias was appraised with design-specific tools and the evidence weighted accordingly. Seventy-one studies across four domains were included: pathophysiology (22 studies), clinical presentation and final diagnosis at follow-up (24 studies), imaging (21 studies), and treatment response (4 studies). Genetically, in one low risk of bias study that stratified EORA by rheumatoid factor status, PMR and seronegative EORA shared HLA-DRB1*13/*14 associations, a pattern distinct from the shared epitope-driven susceptibility of seropositive RA. However, divergent metabolomic signatures suggest different downstream inflammatory mechanisms. An exploratory random-effects meta-analysis yielded a pooled PMR-to-RA reclassification rate of 7% (95% CI 4-12%; 9 studies), narrowing to 4% (95% CI 2-7%) in methodologically robust studies, though rates of reclassification to RA were considerably higher (up to 20%) when patients with undifferentiated polymyalgic presentations were included. Peripheral arthritis occurred in 28% of PMR patients (95% CI 20-35%; 6 studies), with a significant difference between baseline prevalence (21%) and cumulative incidence over follow-up (34%) on subgroup meta-analysis (p = 0.026), and was characteristically transient and glucocorticoid-responsive, whereas persistent synovitis involving wrists and small joints was associated with reclassification to RA. On imaging, evidence from low-to-moderate risk of bias, ultrasound studies showed that shoulder findings overlapped substantially between conditions, whereas bilateral hip synovitis was significantly more frequent in PMR (47% vs 0% in RA), suggesting the hip as a stronger proximal informative site. However, distal joint synovitis demonstrated the highest discriminatory value, with the presence of at least one among RF positivity, hand grey-scale ≥2, or hand power Doppler ≥1 achieving 89% sensitivity and 93% specificity for EORA identification. This review highlights that the distinction between EORA and PMR cannot be reliably established at a single time point and that longitudinal reassessment integrating clinical, serological, and imaging findings remains essential for the differential diagnosis. However, the evidence is limited by clinical and methodological heterogeneity and the predominance of observational designs.

title: Early postnatal brain volumes and two-year cognitive outcomes in preterm infants: An exploratory machine learning study.
abstract: Introduction Premature birth is associated with an increased risk of cognitive and motor developmental problems. Early prediction of these outcomes is crucial for timely intervention and adequate follow-up. This study aimed to predict cognitive and motor outcomes in preterm-born infants using brain volumetric features in combination with clinical and demographic perinatal characteristics, and to compare the performance of three different machine learning algorithms. Methods We acquired quantitative structural brain MRI at approximately 30 weeks postmenstrual age (PMA) and clinical and demographic birth characteristics including gestational age, sex, birthweight, and maternal education level. Machine learning techniques were applied to predict cognitive (N = 63) and motor (N = 41) outcomes at two years corrected age, assessed using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development III, in infants born before 30 weeks gestation. We evaluated the performance of logistic regression, linear support vector classifier (linear SVC), and k-nearest neighbour (KNN). Results Employing volumetric features only, KNN achieved a validation accuracy of 0.64, showing modest predictive power for cognitive outcomes. Adding clinical characteristics did not significantly improve accuracy. The models did not perform better than chance when predicting motor outcomes. Conclusion Volumetric features demonstrated modest predictive ability for cognitive outcomes, and the addition of clinical features did not significantly improve performance. The low to moderate overall validation accuracy underscores, however, the challenges faced in the clinical application of machine learning in neuroimaging. The reliability and clinical applicability of predictions of outcomes from advanced neuroimaging data will largely depend on the quantity and quality of the data, methodological standardisation, and the generalisability of the prediction models.

title: Intrinsic dimension for evaluating and analyzing neural networks for medical image segmentation.
abstract: Background and objective Evaluating medical image segmentation models typically relies on expert annotations, which are scarce, costly, and time-consuming to obtain. Intrinsic dimension (ID), defined as the minimal number of parameters required to describe high-dimensional data, has been shown to correlate with model generalization in classification tasks, but whether this relationship extends to segmentation remains unclear. Methods In this study, we systematically investigate ID as a label-free indicator for evaluating segmentation performance, including the generalization of standard segmentation models and the adaptability of promptable foundation models (i.e., SAM-based models). We also perform a layer-wise ID analysis to characterize variations in latent representation complexity. Furthermore, we propose a novel, computation- and memory-efficient strategy for ID calculation to broaden its applications. Results We reveal the following findings: 1) For standard segmentation, lower ID values of training-sample representations are consistently associated with better generalization performance on unseen test samples, as measured by DSC. 2) For promptable segmentation, test-data ID consistently reflects model adaptability to specific target data compared to entropy, a metric commonly believed to predict performance. 3) Layer-wise ID in segmentation follows an initially increasing and then decreasing pattern, similar to that in classification. Conclusions Our findings suggest the potential of ID as a label-free indicator for assessing the generalization and adaptability of segmentation models, thereby supporting model selection in label-scarce clinical settings.

title: CDPDNet: Integrating text guidance with hybrid vision encoders for medical image segmentation.
abstract: Most publicly available medical segmentation datasets are only partially labeled, with annotations provided for a subset of anatomical structures. When multiple datasets are combined for training, this incomplete annotation poses challenges, as it limits the model's ability to learn shared anatomical representations among datasets. Furthermore, vision-only frameworks often struggle to resolve semantic ambiguities between missing labels and target regions, potentially hindering discriminative performance and cross-dataset consistency. In this study, we proposed a CLIP-DINO Prompt-Driven Segmentation Network (CDPDNet), which combined a self-supervised vision transformer with CLIP-based text embedding and introduced task-specific text prompts to tackle these challenges. Specifically, the framework was constructed upon a convolutional neural network (CNN) and incorporated DINOv2 to extract both fine-grained and global visual features, which were then fused using a multi-head cross-attention module to overcome the limited long-range modeling capability of CNNs. In addition, CLIP-derived text embeddings were projected into the visual space to help model complex relationships among organs and tumors. To further address the partial label challenge and enhance inter-task discriminative capability, a Text-based Task Prompt Generation (TTPG) module that generated task-specific prompts was designed to guide the segmentation. Extensive experiments on multiple medical imaging datasets demonstrated that CDPDNet consistently outperformed existing state-of-the-art segmentation methods. Code and pretrained model are available at: https://github.com/wujiong-hub/CDPDNet.git.

Code and pretrained model are available at: https://github.com/wujiong-hub/CDPDNet.git.

title: RADMorph: A region-aware deformable registration network for organ-specific thoracic CT alignment.
abstract: Deformable image registration plays an important role in radiation therapy, supporting applications such as contour propagation, treatment planning, and motion analysis. However, accurate registration of lung CT images remains challenging in the presence of large respiratory-induced deformations. In this study, we propose RADMorph, a deep learning framework that explicitly models region-dependent motion to improve registration robustness and anatomical consistency under large deformations. RADMorph comprises two key components. The Adaptive Region Feature Encoder (ARFE) learns region-specific motion representations through feature clustering and region-conditioned filtering, while the Region-Centered Displacement Modulator (RCDM) estimates deformation fields by integrating local image similarity with inter-region distance-based modulation. We evaluated RADMorph on multi-center datasets acquired under free-breathing and deep-inspiration breath-hold conditions, as well as on four-dimensional CT datasets. Across these datasets, RADMorph showed competitive overall performance compared with convolutional and transformer-based registration methods, with improvements varying across geometric and intensity-based metrics. The proposed method improved contour propagation and boundary localization for clinically relevant structures in most evaluated settings while reducing global deformation folding. Quantitative evaluations further demonstrated accurate voxel-level correspondence across the evaluated datasets, supporting the potential use of RADMorph in applications that rely on spatial correspondence, such as dose mapping and adaptive radiotherapy. RADMorph integrates region-aware representation learning with distance-modulated deformation estimation to provide a region-informed approach for modeling complex respiratory motion. These characteristics may facilitate more reliable contour transfer and quantitative analysis of dynamic thoracic imaging.

title: Medical Vision Foundation Models: A comprehensive review from technical evolution to clinical translation.
abstract: Medical Vision Foundation Models (MVFMs) mark a shift from task-specific artificial intelligence (AI) toward general-purpose visual intelligence in medical imaging. However, clinical deployment remains constrained by tensions among data availability, technological development, and integration into clinical workflows. To address these issues, this review provides a systematic analysis of the field's evolution from 2019 to 2025. We introduce the Data-Technology-Translation Triad as a unifying conceptual framework to structure the progress, key factors, and challenges of MVFMs. Our analysis traces the field's development and identifies a convergence toward Transformer-based and hybrid architectures, alongside hybrid pre-training paradigms. We present a unified technical framework that covers pre-training strategies, including generative, contrastive, and hybrid learning, as well as adaptation mechanisms such as full fine-tuning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and prompt learning. Furthermore, we examine how data scarcity, heterogeneity, and privacy constraints in medical imaging drive the adoption of self-supervised learning and highlight domain generalization as a critical research direction. Although MVFMs demonstrate strong performance in data-efficient and multi-task settings, their clinical translation is hindered by limited generalization, insufficient interpretability, misalignment with clinical workflows, and regulatory uncertainty. In response, we propose practical directions for developing reliable general-purpose medical vision systems, with emphasis on causal reasoning, dynamic data learning, interactive human-AI collaboration, and coordinated efforts among researchers, clinicians, and regulators. This review provides a structured reference to guide MVFMs from technical validation to clinically effective, reliable, and ethically sound deployment. An updated collection of MVFM papers and related resources is available at our website https://github.com/ice-TuoShui/MVFM-Review.

title: Deep learning-based super-resolution reconstruction for improved image quality in shoulder MRI.
abstract: Purpose To compare the image quality of shoulder Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) using three imaging acquisition or reconstruction approaches-Parallel Imaging (PI), Compressed Sensing (CS), and Deep Learning-Based Super-Resolution Reconstruction (SR)-and to evaluate reader-assessed image quality and preference. Methods A retrospective study included 60 patients (27 males, 33 females; mean age 53.67 ± 12.11 years). Shoulder MRI was performed with PI, CS and SR (reconstructed from CS data) across six sequences. Quantitative and qualitative assessments were conducted by experienced observers. Three radiologists selected clinically preferred sequences after a 2-week washout. Consistency and inter-group comparisons were statistically analyzed. Results The quantitative and qualitative assessment between observers showed good consistency. The SR group showed significantly higher quantitative measurements across all six sequences of structures [e.g. SNR: Supraspinatus tendon SR 14.03 (10.60, 20.26), CS 11.87 (8.39, 15.96), PI 8.75 (5.18, 13.51), P < 0.001] than PI and CS. SR images generally showed lower edge rise distance (ERD) values, significant overall differences among PI, CS, and SR (P < 0.01), Qualitative assessment revealed that SR overall differences among PI, CS and SR, with statistically significant differences (P < 0.001). Furthermore, three reader preference results indicated a preference for SR images that all readers preferred SR images (86 %, 92 %, and 93 %). Conclusion Compared to PI and CS, SR significantly improves image quality in shoulder MRI without increasing acquisition time. SR enhances the visualization of fine anatomical structures, providing improved image quality and supporting its potential application in clinical shoulder MRI.

title: Periprostatic adipose tissue imaging in prostate cancer: Imaging phenotypes, task-specific spatial strategies, and multicompartment integration-a critical review.
abstract: Purpose To appraise how periprostatic adipose tissue (PPAT) is defined, sampled, and evaluated in prostate cancer imaging, with emphasis on spatial strategy, intended clinical use, evidence maturity, and imaging-tissue correspondence. Method We conducted a structured critical review with evidence mapping, supported by PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science searches through August 29, 2026, supplemented by prespecified Google Scholar and citation searches. Two reviewers independently screened records. Reports were mapped by imaging strategy, spatial target, clinical task, evaluation design, reproducibility, cohort overlap, and imaging-tissue correspondence. Results The formal evidence set comprised 113 reports, including 63 clinical imaging reports. Strategies comprised morphometry / computed tomography (CT) attenuation (48 reports), tissue-property / compositional imaging (4), PPAT-focused radiomics (4), and interface / multicompartment modelling (7). Quantitative reproducibility was reported in 19/63 clinical reports. Only two reports underwent independent external evaluation, and neither evaluated a PPAT-only model. Biological and translational evidence supported PPAT as a heterogeneous tumour-adjacent compartment, whereas direct spatially matched imaging-tissue validation remained uncommon. Clinical evidence spanned prebiopsy risk refinement, upgrading or active-surveillance reclassification, local extension and surgical planning, prognosis, treatment-related outcomes, and nodal and metastatic assessment; most reports lacked independent evaluation. Conclusions PPAT imaging is best regarded as a set of spatially defined, task-specific phenotypes rather than a single biomarker. Current evidence positions PPAT as a candidate adjunct to established clinical and intraprostatic imaging information. Clinical adoption will require reproducible definitions and measurements, task-matched assessment of incremental value, independent external evaluation, and prospective evidence of decision impact.

title: Photon-counting CT based vestibular aqueduct trajectory analysis for the assessment of Ménière's disease endotypes and hearing loss.
abstract: Background Ménière's disease (MD) is a heterogeneous inner ear disorder, and imaging-based endotype identification may inform prognosis and personalized management. The vestibular aqueduct (VA) is a candidate imaging biomarker, and photon-counting CT (PCCT) offers high-resolution depiction of temporal bone microanatomy. This study evaluated PCCT-derived VA morphometric parameters as imaging biomarkers for MD endotype identification and hearing loss assessment. Methods In this retrospective study, 106 patients (212 ears) underwent temporal bone PCCT and 3.0-T 3D-FLAIR MRI. PCCT parameters included angular trajectory of the VA (ATVA), VA visibility grade, morphologic subtype, midpoint width, VA length, and posterior semicircular canal-posterior fossa distance. Two neuroradiologists independently evaluated all images. Diagnostic performance for six clinically motivated tasks was assessed by AUC with leave-one-patient-out cross-validation (LOPOCV); associations with pure-tone average (PTA) were evaluated by multivariable linear regression with cluster-robust standard errors. Results Interobserver agreement was excellent (ICC, 0.84-0.91). VA visibility grading identified the hypoplastic endotype with an AUC of 0.860 (LOPOCV, 0.812); combined VA morphology and midpoint width distinguished the degenerated endotype with an AUC of 0.784 (LOPOCV, 0.736). Multivariable regression identified ATVA as an independent PTA predictor (β = 0.238, p = 0.023). Conclusions PCCT-derived VA morphometric parameters enabled MD endotype identification despite clinical heterogeneity and were associated with hearing loss severity, supporting their potential role as imaging biomarkers for MD management.

title: Nursing management of postoperative hemorrhagic shock: A case study in intensive care.
abstract: Introduction Postoperative hemorrhagic shock is a time-critical complication associated with high morbidity and mortality, particularly in older surgical patients, requiring rapid, coordinated management in the intensive care unit (ICU). This case report describes specialized nursing management guided by the International Classification for Nursing Practice (ICNP®/CIPE®) and Benner's Clinical Wisdom Theory. Case presentation An 89-year-old woman underwent emergency gastrojejunostomy for intestinal obstruction and subsequently developed hemorrhagic shock with profound anemia (hemoglobin nadir 5.8 g/dL), severe hyperlactatemia (12 mmol/L), hypothermia (33.6 °C), peripheral hypoperfusion, and hypotension (mean arterial pressure <65 mmHg). She required orotracheal intubation, invasive mechanical ventilation, and deep sedation. Diagnostic reassessment included serial hemoglobin and arterial blood gas analyses, lactate trending, invasive hemodynamic monitoring, and surgical re-exploration with intraoperative upper endoscopy, which suggested an upper gastrointestinal source (suspected Mallory-Weiss type lesion) treated endoscopically. Nursing priorities, structured using ICNP®, focused on perfusion restoration and correction of the lethal triad (hypothermia, acidosis, coagulopathy), multimodal analgesia, continuous monitoring, prevention bundles (infection and pressure injury prevention), and structured family communication. Discussion The patient progressively stabilized, with hemoglobin increasing to 9.6 g/dL, lactate decreasing to <1 mmol/L, normothermia recovery, discontinuation of vasopressors, and no documented ICU-acquired complications during the ICU stay. This case highlights how standardized nursing language (ICNP®/CIPE®), combined with advanced clinical reasoning and evidence-based ICU bundles, can improve the structure, traceability, and continuity of nursing care in postoperative hemorrhagic shock.

title: Quantifying digital volume correlation strain uncertainty at the bone-pedicle screw interface: an ex-vivo zero-strain analysis.
abstract: Pedicle screws are essential for postoperative construct stability in spinal fusion surgeries. However, screw loosening remains a common clinical complication, often linked to excessive loading that induces damaging trabecular bone strains surrounding the pedicle screw. Toward improving pre-clinical assessment of pedicle screw fixation, this study combines micro-CT imaging, U-Net deep learning segmentation, and digital volume correlation (DVC) techniques to quantify the errors associated with measuring full-field strains at the screw-bone interface under nominal zero-strain conditions. Pedicle screws were surgically implanted into six human lumbar vertebrae specimens. Each specimen underwent micro-CT imaging. For three specimens, paired unloaded scans were acquired and analyzed using a standard DVC uncertainty workflow. To mitigate local bone-metal artifacts, bone segmentation was performed using a U-Net model, and segmentation accuracy was quantified using the Sørensen-Dice similarity coefficient. The U-Net model reproduced manual segmentations with high fidelity (average Dice = 0.94 ± 0.01). DVC accuracy and precision depended on the spatial resolution of strain measurement; at a DVC spatial resolution of 1.8 mm, strain estimates around the screw were reliable with low error (accuracy = 387 ± 110 µε; precision = 222 ± 82 µε). This study establishes the feasibility of a micro-CT-based DVC workflow and characterizes the strain measurement errors within trabecular bone surrounding pedicle screws using a zero-strain analysis. This workflow provides a foundation for future studies involving loaded tests, further optimization of segmentation to suppress artifacts, and validation across larger cohorts and implant designs.

title: A Visual LGE Extent Cutoff for Mortality Risk Stratification in Ischemic Cardiomyopathy.
abstract: Background Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) extent has been linked to adverse outcomes in ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM). While quantitative methods of LGE assessment are widely accepted, semi-quantitative methods remain debated but still hold value. This study aimed to determine an optimal LGE segments cutoff for ICM patients with left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) <50% in a large bicentric cohort. Methods This bicentric retrospective French study included 3,591 patients with ICM (defined by prior myocardial infarction and/or coronary revascularization), LVEF <50%, and ischemic-LGE on cardiovascular magnetic resonance performed between 2008 and 2022. Ischemic LGE extent was assessed semi-quantitatively using the 17-segment model. An optimal cutoff for LGE extent was derived in the derivation cohort (Center 1, N=2,900) using a conditional inference tree and externally validated in an independent cohort (Center 2, N=691). The primary outcome was all-cause mortality. Prognostic performance was compared between a conventional model based on LVEF ≤35% alone and a combined model integrating LVEF ≤35% with the newly identified ischemic-LGE cutoff. Model discrimination and reclassification were assessed using Harrell's C-index, continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Results During a median follow-up of 9 years, 549 patients (15.3%) died. The optimal cutoff of visual LGE extent to predict mortality was 5 segments. Patients with high ischemic LGE extent (>5 segments) had a markedly increased risk of all-cause mortality compared with those with ≤5 segments (adjusted hazard ratio, 3.8; 95% CI: 3.0-4.8; p<0.001). Survival discrimination according to this cutoff was consistent across derivation and validation cohorts. Compared with the conventional LVEF ≤35% model alone, the combined model integrating the >5 ischemic-LGE segment cutoff significantly improved risk discrimination and patient reclassification (ΔC-index: +16%; continuous NRI: +36%; IDI: +4%; all p<0.001). Conclusion In patients with ICM, reduced LVEF (<50%), and detectable ischemic LGE, a visually assessed segment-based cutoff of >5 ischemic-LGE segments was independently associated with all-cause mortality and validated in an independent second-center cohort. This pragmatic, software-independent assessment may complement conventional risk stratification, although prospective studies are required before integration into clinical decision-making.

title: Streamline pathology foundation model by cross-magnification distillation.
abstract: Foundation models (FM) have transformed computational pathology but remain computationally prohibitive for clinical deployment due to their massive parameter counts and high-magnification processing requirements. Here, we introduce XMAG, a lightweight FM developed through cross-magnification distillation that transfers knowledge from a state-of-the-art 20x magnification teacher to an efficient 5x magnification student architecture. XMAG employs a compact backbone and operates entirely at 5x, requiring 11.3 times fewer patches per whole slide image (WSI) compared to existing approaches. Our novel distillation framework incorporates dual-level knowledge transfer, aligning both global image representations and local spatial features across magnification levels through carefully designed projection heads and spatial token mapping. We trained XMAG on 3.49 million images curated from publicly available datasets and evaluated performance across seven clinically relevant histopathology analysis tasks spanning multiple cancer types. Across four WSI-level classification tasks, XMAG achieved an average AUC within 1% of substantially larger foundation models while delivering up to 29.5-fold faster encoder-level processing, corresponding to an encoder throughput of 8.8 WSIs per minute in a controlled patch-encoding benchmark. We also found that performance differences remained task-dependent, with larger gaps observed for fine-grained tasks such as ISUP grading and patch-level phenotyping. We further explore end-to-end XMAG training as a direction for task-specific adaptation of the compact model. These results suggest that cross-magnification distillation is a promising strategy for developing efficient low-magnification pathology foundation models and may support more scalable WSI analysis in computationally constrained research and translational settings.

title: Applied nutritional investigation determinants of lower quadriceps skeletal muscle measured by ultrasound at ICU admission: a cross-sectional analysis.
abstract: Background Low skeletal muscle (SM) is common at ICU admission and is associated with worse prognosis. Early identification of at-risk patients is essential, but determinants of low SM in critically ill patients remains unclear. Objective To identify sociodemographic, nutritional, and clinical characteristics associated with low SM at ICU admission. Methods This cross-sectional analysis included critically ill patients ≥18 years admitted within 24 hours. Sociodemographic and nutritional data were obtained through anamnesis, while clinical data were extracted from records. Quadriceps muscle layer thickness (QMLT) was measured using a B-mode US. Lower QMLT was defined as values below the sex-specific 25th percentile of the sample. Binary logistic regression was performed. Results 399 patients were included (age 61.4 ± 14.9 years; 56.6% male). Older age (OR = 1.02; CI 95% 1.0-1.04), previous unintentional weight loss (OR = 1.64; CI 95% 1.03-2.61), reduced food intake before admission (OR = 2.32; CI 95% 1.44-3.74), and pressure injuries (OR = 1.83; CI 95% 1.05-3.20) were associated with low QMLT. However, in multivariate analysis, only older age (OR = 1.02; CI 95% 1.00-1.04) and reduced food intake (OR = 2.26; CI 95% 1.22-4.18) remained independent determinants. Conclusion Older age and reduced food intake were independently associated with lower QMLT at ICU admission. These findings highlight the need for early screening and targeted strategies to mitigate muscle loss and improve outcomes in critically ill patients.
